signals.title: Feature Request: Native Scheduling for Opencode
signals.text: ## Summary Add native scheduling capabilities to opencode (e.g., `opencode schedule --cron '0 9 * * *' --skill recruiter-response`). ## Motivation Currently, users must rely on OS-level tools like `crontab` or SystemD timers to run recurring tasks. This creates friction and platform dependency (e.g., Windows vs. macOS/Linux). A native scheduler would improve the user experience for autonomous agents. ## Proposed Solution - Add a `schedule` command. - Allow defining schedules via cron syntax or natural language (if possible). - Persist schedules in the opencode configuration. - Run a background daemon to handle scheduled tasks (could leverage `opencode serve`).

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add configurable timeout parameter to the Task tool
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request The Task tool (used to dispatch subagents like `explore` and `general`) has no timeout parameter. Subagents can hang for 5–15+ minutes on tasks that should complete in 15–30 seconds, blocking the entire conversation with no way for the caller to recover programmatically. The Bash tool already supports an optional `timeout` parameter (in milliseconds). The Task tool should have the same capability. **Proposed changes:** 1. Add an optional `timeout` parameter to the Task tool schema (milliseconds, consistent with Bash tool). 2. Set a reasonable default timeout (e.g., 120,000 ms / 2 minutes) when none is specified. 3. On timeout, return a structured timeout error so the calling agent can fall back — retry with a smaller scope, do the work directly, or inform the user. **Why this matters:** - There is currently no workaround. The caller agent waits indefinitely and the user must manually abort. - Codebases with AI rules (e.g., "set explicit timeout per request," "never wait indefinitely") cannot enforce those rules on Task tool calls because the parameter doesn't exist. - This is distinct from the async/non-blocking dispatch request in #15069. That issue proposes a fundamentally different execution model. This request is narrower: just add a timeout so synchronous Task calls don't hang forever. **Note:** Supersedes #15072, which was not created using the required feature request template.

signals.title: Runaway /tmp .589*-00000000.so artifacts can exhaust disk during long-running usage
signals.text: ## Problem During long-running usage, temporary files under `/tmp` accumulate rapidly with names like: - `.589<hex>-00000000.so` These can grow unbounded and exhaust root disk space. ## Environment - Linux host - OpenCode CLI/serve usage over long sessions ## Observed Behavior - `/tmp` grew to tens of GB from this pattern alone - files continued to appear over time - disk exhaustion caused service instability and I/O errors ## Reproduction Pattern 1. Run OpenCode continuously with multiple active sessions/plugins/tools 2. Observe `/tmp` over time 3. Count matching files: - `ls /tmp | grep -E '^\\.589[0-9a-f]+-00000000\\.so$' | wc -l` ## Expected Behavior - temporary runtime artifacts should be cleaned automatically - no unbounded growth in `/tmp` ## Suggested Fix Directions - ensure deterministic cleanup for generated temp `.so` artifacts - add lifecycle hooks for cleanup on process exit and crash paths - consider bounded temp storage / periodic internal cleanup - add debug metrics/logging for temp artifact creation and cleanup

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Ephemeral Sub-Agent Teams (parallel multi-agent orchestration)
signals.text: # [FEATURE]: Ephemeral Sub-Agent Teams (parallel multi-agent orchestration) ## Feature hasn't been suggested before This builds on the ideas in #12711 and #19215 but proposes a different approach: **ephemeral, scoped teams** that are created for a task and destroyed when done — no persistent team state, no new DB tables, no file-based coordination. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Problem The `task` tool spawns sub-agents sequentially — each runs in its own session, returns a result, and that's it. There's no way for sub-agents to: 1. **Run in parallel** on independent subtasks 2. **Communicate** with each other during execution 3. **Coordinate** via a lead agent that assigns work, monitors progress, and merges results Claude Code's "agent-teams" capability solves this. OpenCode should too. ### What's different from #12711 and #19215 Both proposals add persistent team infrastructure (file-based or DB-backed). That's a large surface area with recovery logic, TUI integration, and ongoing state management. This proposal takes a lighter approach: | Aspect | #12711 / #19215 | This proposal | |--------|-----------------|---------------| | Lifecycle | Persistent teams that survive restarts | Ephemeral — created per-task, auto-cleaned | | Storage | JSON files / new SQLite tables | Existing sessions + in-memory coordination | | Recovery | Complex reconciliation | None needed — if parent dies, children abort | | Scope | 9+ new tools | 1 new tool (`team`) + 1 coordination module | | Communication | Cross-session message injection | Shared message bus scoped to team lifetime | ### Proposed design **One new tool: `team`** ```typescript z.object({ description: z.string(), tasks: z.array(z.object({ agent: z.string(), prompt: z.string(), id: z.string().optional(), // for dependency references depends: z.array(z.string()).optional(), })), concurrency: z.number().optional(), // default: all parallel }) ``` The LLM calls `team` with a batch of tasks. The tool: 1. Creates child sessions (like `task` does today) 2. Runs them in parallel via `Promise.all` (respecting `depends` for ordering) 3. Pipes results back as a combined output 4. Cleans up — child sessions remain browsable but the coordination state is gone **Optional: inter-agent messaging** A lightweight `Bus`-based channel scoped to the team's lifetime. Agents can post messages visible to siblings. This enables patterns like "agent A produces a schema, agent B consumes it" without round-tripping through the lead. ### Why ephemeral - **No new persistence** — uses existing Session infrastructure - **No recovery logic** — parent abort signal cascades to children (already works in `task.ts`) - **No new TUI** — child sessions already show in the session hierarchy - **Minimal blast radius** — opt-in via `experimental.team_tool`, same pattern as `batch_tool` ### Use cases - Parallel file analysis (explore agent per directory) - Concurrent implementation + test writing - Multi-model review (run same prompt through different providers) - Research fan-out (multiple search queries simultaneously)
signals.author: lleontor705

signals.title: Headless opencode serve still extracts libopentui.so into /tmp on every start, causing temp artifact buildup
signals.text: ### Description `opencode serve` is documented as a headless server, but on Linux it still extracts a bundled native OpenTUI shared library (`libopentui.so`) into `/tmp` during startup. In long-running environments where `opencode serve` is restarted periodically, this causes repeated creation of hidden temp artifacts such as: - `/tmp/.58afeffabbf7dede-00000000.so` - `/tmp/.58afffdf9b3fffef-00000000.so` Observed properties: - each file is about 4.2 MB - filenames are randomized - file content is identical across runs - ELF `SONAME` is `libopentui.so` - the file is mapped directly by the `opencode serve` process itself - the artifact is created at startup time, before `pyright-langserver` starts This means the issue is not primarily about language-server activity. It appears to come from the standalone `opencode` binary extracting a bundled native library even for `serve`. ### Why this is a problem For headless server deployments, this behavior is surprising and operationally expensive: - `/tmp` accumulates many hidden `.so` files over time - repeated restarts create new copies with different names - cleanup is hard to automate safely in shared `/tmp` - the behavior is especially awkward for long-running service environments, where `serve` is used without any terminal UI ### What I verified On Linux, I verified that: 1. `opencode serve` starts first 2. the temp `.so` appears immediately after startup 3. `pyright-langserver` starts much later 4. `lsof` and `/proc/<pid>/maps` show the `.so` is mapped by the `opencode serve` process 5. the extracted file reports `SONAME: libopentui.so` ### Expected behavior At least one of the following would be preferable: 1. `opencode serve` should avoid loading or extracting OpenTUI native libraries entirely when running in headless mode 2. the extracted native library should be cleaned up automatically on normal shutdown 3. extracted files should be reused from a stable cache path instead of creating a new randomized temp file on each start 4. documentation for `serve` should explicitly call out the `BUN_TMPDIR` requirement/workaround for service deployments ### Suggested improvements #### Preferred - split headless/server builds from TUI-capable builds, so `opencode serve` does not carry OpenTUI runtime baggage at all #### Acceptable - reuse a deterministic cache location for bundled native libs - unlink temp artifacts after successful load when possible - provide an explicit server/runtime flag or documented environment variable strategy for temp extraction ### Workaround `BUN_TMPDIR` helps redirect the extraction location, but it does not solve the underlying accumulation behavior. Example: ```bash BUN_TMPDIR=/var/lib/opencode-bun-tmp opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 34876 ``` This is useful operationally, but it still feels like a workaround rather than the correct headless-server behavior. ### Version Observed on the latest release at the time of filing: `v1.3.7` ### Environment - OS: Linux - mode: `opencode serve` - deployment style: long-running headless service
signals.author: liujuanjuan1984

signals.title: [FEATURE]: @opencode-ai/slack — support connecting to an existing remote OpenCode server
signals.text: - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. `@opencode-ai/slack` currently always spawns a local OpenCode server via `createOpencode()`. It should support connecting to an existing remote server when an environment variable (e.g. `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL`) is set. ## Problem The Slack bot in `packages/slack/src/index.ts` hardcodes server creation: ```typescript const opencode = await createOpencode({ port: 0 }) ``` This means the Slack bot and the OpenCode server must run in the same process/container. There's no way to point the bot at a server running elsewhere. ## Use case In Kubernetes environments, OpenCode runs as a persistent server (via `opencode serve`) inside a cluster. The Slack bot needs to run as a separate Deployment that connects to this existing server over the internal network. The current architecture makes this impossible without forking the package. This is the same pattern already discussed in: - #15801 — GitHub Action `--attach` to remote server - #7629 — Desktop app connecting to existing server - #9099 — Exporting `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` The SDK already exposes `createOpencodeClient({ baseUrl })` for exactly this purpose — the Slack bot just doesn't use it. ## Proposed change ```typescript let client: OpencodeClient let server: { url: string; close(): void } | undefined if (process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL) { client = createOpencodeClient({ baseUrl: process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL }) } else { const opencode = await createOpencode({ port: 0 }) client = opencode.client server = opencode.server } ``` Optionally also support `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` / `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` for authenticated servers (consistent with existing `opencode attach` auth). No breaking changes — default behavior is preserved when the env var is not set. ## Why this matters The Slack bot is one of the simplest and most compelling integrations in the OpenCode ecosystem. Letting it connect to a remote server unlocks: - **Kubernetes-native deployment** — separate bot pod from server pod, each scaling independently - **Shared context** — multiple Slack threads can share the same server's loaded repos/context - **Enterprise deployment** — server behind VPN, bot exposed to Slack via Socket Mode (no public URL needed) - **Multi-interface** — same server serves the web UI, CLI (`opencode attach`), and Slack bot simultaneously

signals.title: [BUG] Archive action causes 4+ hours of session data loss on Windows Desktop
signals.text: ### Description When clicking the "Archive" button in OpenCode Desktop for Windows, all conversation history from the current session that hasn't been persisted to the database is permanently lost. This is a critical data loss bug. ## Impact - Severity: Critical (data loss) - Affected Users: All Windows Desktop users - Data Lost: 4+ hours of conversation history (in my case) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open OpenCode Desktop on Windows 10/11 2. Start a new conversation and chat for several hours 3. Do NOT manually save/export the conversation 4. Click the "Archive" button in the session list 5. The current session disappears from the list 6. All messages from ~17:57 to ~21:40 are permanently lost ## Expected Behavior - Archiving a session should save all pending messages to the database first - Archived sessions should be recoverable via an "Unarchive" function - Users should be warned if there are unsaved messages before archiving ## Actual Behavior - Session data in memory is NOT persisted before archiving - No confirmation dialog warns about unsaved data - No way to recover the archived session - Database shows no record of the lost conversation ## Technical Evidence ### Database Query Results Queried `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: ```sql SELECT id, slug, title, time_updated FROM session ORDER BY time_updated DESC LIMIT 10; ``` | Session ID | Title | Last Updated (Local Time) | |------------|-------|--------------------------| | ses_2adb34a58ffelj8oJzw2806lGG | GitHub 项目本地部署与启动流程 | 2026-04-03 14:49:12 | | ses_2ac431abcffefonOJboRolkgoG | 恢复归档会话记录 | 2026-04-03 14:37:59 | | ses_2ad40870affew5ZoDh95e1eu2N | T2: 禁用危险 Sandbox 参数 | 2026-04-03 13:44:49 | All sessions were last updated BEFORE 17:00, but I was actively chatting until 21:40. ### File System Analysis Checked `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session_diff/`: - All session diff files are empty (2 bytes, content: `[]`) - No session data persisted between 17:57-21:40 ### Timeline | Time | Event | |------|-------| | 14:49 | Last session saved to database | | 17:57 | Started new conversation (NOT in database) | | 21:40 | Clicked "Archive" button | | 21:40+ | 4+ hours of conversation history lost | ## Root Cause Analysis Based on source code review and database analysis: 1. Session auto-save mechanism is broken - Messages are not being persisted to the database in real-time 2. Archive action does not trigger a save - Clicking archive should flush pending messages first 3. No warning dialog - Users are not warned about unsaved data before archiving 4. No recovery mechanism - Archived sessions cannot be recovered ## Suggested Fixes ### Immediate (Critical) 1. Add confirmation dialog before archiving if there are unsaved messages 2. Force save pending messages before executing archive action 3. Add warning toast if archive is attempted with pending data ### Long-term 1. Implement proper session persistence - Auto-save messages every N seconds 2. Add unarchive functionality - Allow users to recover archived sessions 3. Add session backup - Create backup before destructive operations ## Workarounds (for users) Until this is fixed, users should: 1. Regularly export conversations using `/export` command (Ctrl+X X) 2. Avoid clicking "Archive" button until the bug is fixed 3. Use TUI version (`opencode` command) - community PR #13961 adds archive/unarchive support ## Related Issues - #15980 - 希望添加「恢复归档会话」的功能 - #15677 - 误操作点到归档了，如何能回撤这个操作 - #12888 - 当一个对话被"归档"，要去哪里找回它 - #16000 - [FEATURE]: Unarchive session ## Related PRs - #13961 - feat: add session archive/unarchive support to TUI - #16212 - feat(session): add archive undo + unarchive command ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal OpenCode Desktop App

signals.title: `opencode run --format json` extracts libopentui.so to /tmp on every invocation, causing unbounded disk growth
signals.text: ### Description ### Problem Every invocation of `opencode` — including headless modes like `opencode run --format json` and `opencode serve` — extracts an identical copy of `libopentui.so` (~4.3 MB) into `/tmp` with a randomized filename. The file is never cleaned up on process exit. In environments where opencode is called frequently (e.g., as a coding agent backend via `opencode run --format json`, or with oh-my-opencode background agents), this causes `/tmp` to grow by **gigabytes per hour** and eventually exhausts root disk space. ### Observed behavior ``` $ ls -la /tmp/.fcbc*.so | head -3 -rw-r--r-- 1 user users 4467856 Apr 7 18:59 /tmp/.fcbcce070aa9c41f-00000000.so -rw-r--r-- 1 user users 4467856 Apr 7 18:59 /tmp/.fcbcce071be8fd7f-00000000.so -rw-r--r-- 1 user users 4467856 Apr 7 18:59 /tmp/.fcbcce071bebfe2d-00000000.so $ ls /tmp/.fcbc*.so | wc -l 5881 $ md5sum /tmp/.fcbc*.so | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u b937f51f51f919d80cdbb94e5486f51f # all 5881 files are identical ``` 5881 identical copies = **~25 GB** consumed in a single day. `strace` confirms: each invocation creates a new file, writes 4,467,856 bytes of ELF data, mmaps it, and **never calls unlink** on exit: ``` openat(13, ".fcbcff3fbbabc6fd-00000000.so", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC, 0644) = 14 write(14, "\177ELF\2\1\1\0...", 4467856) = 4467856 close(14) openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/.fcbcff3fbbabc6fd-00000000.so", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 14 mmap(NULL, 5034944, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_DENYWRITE, 14, 0) = 0x... # process exits — zero unlink calls ``` ### Two independent root causes #### 1. Embedded Bun runtime is v1.2.8, which has a known temp file leak OpenCode (tested across versions 1.2.27 through 1.3.17) embeds **Bun v1.2.8** as its standalone runtime. This version has a known bug where `resolveEmbeddedFile()` in [`ModuleLoader.zig`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/bun.js/ModuleLoader.zig#L33-L71) creates a new randomly-named temp file on every call and never cleans it up. This was **fixed in Bun v1.2.13** ([oven-sh/bun#19550](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/19550)) — the fix adds automatic deletion of temp files on process exit. **Upgrading the embedded Bun to >= v1.2.13 would resolve the leak.** Verification: ```bash # Every opencode version tested embeds the same broken Bun: $ strings opencode-linux-x64@1.2.27/bin/opencode | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 1.2.8 $ strings opencode-linux-x64@1.3.17/bin/opencode | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 1.2.8 ``` #### 2. `opencode run --format json` loads opentui unnecessarily Even in headless/non-TUI mode (`--format json`, `serve`), opencode imports the opentui module, which eagerly calls `dlopen()` on `libopentui.so` at the top level ([`zig.ts:3881-3884`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/main/packages/core/src/zig.ts)): ```typescript // Eager loading at module level — runs regardless of whether TUI is needed try { opentuiLib = new FFIRenderLib(opentuiLibPath) } catch (error) {} ``` This means every `opencode run --format json` call triggers the full native lib extraction + dlopen chain, even though no terminal rendering occurs. **Conditionally importing opentui only in TUI mode would eliminate the extraction entirely for headless use cases.** ### Impact - Production servers running `opencode serve` accumulate temp files on every restart - Platforms using `opencode run --format json` as a coding agent backend (one extraction per user message) see steady disk growth - Users have reported **60+ GB** consumed overnight ([#6523](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6523)) - At least one user has abandoned opencode due to this issue ### Suggested fixes 1. **Upgrade embedded Bun to >= v1.2.13** — This is the most impactful fix. Bun v1.2.13 automatically deletes extracted temp files on process exit ([oven-sh/bun#19550](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/19550)). 2. **Skip opentui import in headless modes** — When running with `--format json` or as `serve`, conditionally skip the opentui module import to avoid the native lib extraction entirely. This would also improve startup time for headless invocations. ### Related issues | Repo | Issue | Title | |------|-------|-------| | **oven-sh/bun** | [#19550](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/19550) | Single-file executable doesn't clean up temporary .node files in /tmp (**fixed in v1.2.13**) | | **anomalyco/opentui** | [#649](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/649) | Ignores TMPDIR and fails when /tmp is mounted as noexec | | **anomalyco/opentui** | [#355](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/355) | Remove top-level await to enable bytecode compilation | | **anomalyco/opencode** | [#6523](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6523) | opencode creates identical temp files everytime it runs | | **anomalyco/opencode** | [#13479](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13479) | /tmp fills up after three days of usage | | **anomalyco/opencode** | [#16996](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/16996) | Runaway /tmp .so artifacts can exhaust disk | | **anomalyco/opencode** | [#20043](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20043) | Headless opencode serve still extracts libopentui.so | ### Environment - OpenCode: 1.3.17 (also reproduced on 1.2.27, 1.3.0, 1.3.13) - Embedded Bun: v1.2.8 - OS: Linux 5.10 x86_64 - opentui: 0.1.87 (bundled) ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: [FEATURE]: persistent daemon agent for workspace context with push/pull coordination
signals.text: ## Verification - [x] I searched existing issues first - [x] This is a feature/design request, not an implementation PR ## Description I’d like OpenCode to support a persistent background daemon agent that runs alongside the main agent for a workspace. The main idea is to introduce a first-class background agent that stays alive during the session and can exchange information with the main agent through both pull and push communication. ## Core concept A daemon agent should be able to: - run continuously in the background for the current workspace - observe long-lived workspace state - maintain structured memory/context that should not be recomputed repeatedly - communicate with the main agent through: - pull: the main agent asks the daemon for current state, summaries, or recommendations - push: the daemon proactively informs the main agent when meaningful events occur ## Why this is useful The main agent is usually optimized for the immediate task in front of it. During longer sessions, it can lose track of operational context that changes in parallel. A daemon agent would act like durable workspace intelligence: always on, low-noise, and able to feed the main agent the right information at the right time. ## One concrete business scenario: multi-repo workspace tracking For example, I often work in a top-level project that contains multiple child Git repositories. In that scenario, the daemon agent could continuously maintain per-repo information such as: - current branch - whether the branch has already been merged upstream - dirty/clean state - ahead/behind status - detected language / stack - how lint / test / build should be run - environment hints such as “use `uv run`”, “use `make test`”, “use `pnpm`”, etc. This would help avoid common failures like: - only noticing very late that the current branch has already been merged upstream and a new branch should have been created - using the wrong Python command path because the repo expects `uv` - repeatedly having to remind the agent how each sub-repo should be linted or tested ## Important clarification The multi-repo Git example is just one concrete use case. The actual feature request is broader: I’m asking for a general daemon-agent mechanism with ongoing coordination between background and foreground agents. ## Possible UX Any of these would work: - automatically start a daemon agent when entering a workspace - expose a command for the main agent to query daemon state - allow the daemon to push important events into the main thread - show daemon-maintained summaries in a side panel or status view ## Minimal acceptance criteria - OpenCode can run a persistent background daemon agent for a workspace - the daemon can maintain state over time rather than acting like a one-shot helper - the main agent can pull structured information from the daemon - the daemon can push important events back to the main agent - repo/Git awareness can be implemented as one valuable use case of this general mechanism This would make OpenCode feel much more capable in real polyrepo workflows, where persistent operational awareness matters as much as immediate code editing.

signals.title: opencode serve leaks ~14GB/hour of .so files in /tmp due to non-pooled ripgrep Workers
signals.text: ## Summary `opencode serve` causes unbounded disk growth in `/tmp` by creating and destroying ripgrep Workers for every file search/list operation. Each Worker triggers Bun to extract the embedded `libopentui.so` (~4.3MB on Linux x64) to `/tmp` with a unique filename, but these files are never cleaned up. ## Root cause Two contributing factors: ### 1. Ripgrep Workers are created and destroyed per-operation (opencode side) In `packages/opencode/src/file/ripgrep.ts`, both `searchWorker()` and `filesWorker()` follow a create-use-destroy pattern: ```typescript // Line 283 - new Worker every call function worker() { return target().pipe( Effect.flatMap((file) => Effect.sync(() => new Worker(file, { env: env() }))) ) } // searchWorker: acquire → use → release(terminate) Effect.acquireUseRelease( worker(), (w) => /* use */, (w) => Effect.sync(() => w.terminate()), ) ``` Every file search, file listing, or grep operation creates a fresh Worker, which is terminated immediately after. ### 2. Bun compiled binary extracts native modules per Worker (Bun side) When running as a compiled binary, each `new Worker()` extracts embedded native modules to `/tmp` with unique hash-based filenames. These are not cleaned up on `worker.terminate()`. (Reported separately: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/29585) ## Impact - **File size**: ~4.3 MB each (`.so` on Linux x64) - **Rate**: ~9 files / 10 seconds under active use → **~14 GB/hour** - **Real-world scenario**: fills a 300 GB partition in ~19 hours - **Stealth**: files are dot-prefixed (hidden) so `ls` does not show them, only `ls -a` or `find` ## Suggested fix **Pool the ripgrep Workers** instead of creating/destroying per operation. Since the Worker is stateless (receives search args via `postMessage`), a simple pool of 1-2 persistent Workers would eliminate the leak entirely: ```typescript // Instead of creating a new Worker per call, keep a persistent one: const workerPool = lazy(() => new Worker(file, { env: env() })) ``` This would also improve performance by avoiding Worker startup overhead on every file operation. ## Environment - **opencode**: v1.4.11 (`opencode serve --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0`) - **OS**: Ubuntu Linux x64 - **Runtime**: Bun compiled binary - **Native module**: `@opentui/core-linux-x64` `libopentui.so` loaded via `bun:ffi` `dlopen()` ## Workaround ```bash # Periodic cleanup cron */30 * * * * find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name ".*-00000000.so" -mmin +5 -delete ``` ## Reproduction 1. Deploy `opencode serve` on a Linux server 2. Use it actively (trigger file searches, grep, file listings) 3. Monitor: `watch -n 5 "find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name '.*-00000000.so' | wc -l"` 4. Observe ~50+ new `.so` files per minute

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Enhance Input/Output Structure of "experimental.chat.system.transform" and "experimental.chat.messages.transform" Hooks for Better Usability
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Version Current version: `1.14.48` ## Environment Pure code logic, environment-agnostic. ## Problem Description While developing an OpenCode plugin, I discovered the `experimental.chat.system.transform` and `experimental.chat.messages.transform` hooks. I was excited because they seemed perfect for fine-tuning system prompts and message history for each prompt. However, I quickly realized they didn't meet my expectations due to a shared limitation: the Input and Output data structures are insufficient. See the details below: ### experimental.chat.system.transform **Parameters**: - input: `{ sessionID?: string; model: Model }` - output: `{ system: string[] }` **Callers**: - Caller 1: `session/llm.ts:118-121` (Normal LLM call) - Caller 2: `agent/agent.ts:451` (Agent generation, without session context) ### experimental.chat.messages.transform **Parameters**: - input: `{}` - output: `{ messages: { info: Message; parts: Part[] }[] }` **Callers**: - Caller 1: `session/prompt.ts:1587` (Normal LLM call) - Caller 2: `session/compaction.ts:411` (During compaction) ### Common Issue `sessionID` and `messageID` are important pieces of data for determining whether and how we should process the system prompt and message history for the current prompt. I suggest adding them to the input structure. (Of course, due to the differences in callers, it is acceptable for these fields to be optional/undefined in certain cases.) ## Improvement Suggestions ### experimental.chat.system.transform **Parameters**: - input: `{ sessionID?: string; messageID?: string; model: Model }` - output: `{ system: string[] }` ### experimental.chat.messages.transform **Parameters**: - input: `{ sessionID?: string; messageID?: string; model: Model }` - output: `{ messages: { info: Message; parts: Part[] }[] }` ## Feasibility Assessment Since these are experimental hooks, the impact of the change is minimal. The proposed changes are backward compatible and require very little code modification, making them highly feasible.

signals.title: bug(session): infinite compaction loop when compression fails to reduce context
signals.text: ## Bug Description The session loop in `prompt.ts` can enter an infinite compaction loop: ``` overflow detected → compact → still overflow → compact → ... (infinite) ``` This happens when compaction fails to reduce the context below the token limit — for example, when compression state is lost, messages are inherently uncompressable, or the compression plugin returns an error. The loop spins indefinitely consuming API credits without making progress. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Have a session with large context that triggers overflow 2. If compaction fails or doesn't reduce tokens enough, the loop retries indefinitely 3. Observe continuous API calls with no progress ## Root Cause The `runLoop` function has two paths that trigger compaction and `continue` without any guard: 1. **Overflow check**: after each step, if `compaction.isOverflow()` returns true, it calls `compaction.create()` and continues — but the next iteration sees the same overflow and repeats. 2. **Compact result**: when the provider returns `"compact"` as the result, it calls `compaction.create()` and continues — same infinite loop if compaction doesn't actually reduce context. Neither path has a retry counter or break condition. ## Expected Behavior After a reasonable number of compaction attempts (e.g., 2), the loop should break and return an error to the user, rather than spinning indefinitely.

signals.title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time
signals.text: ### Description ## Title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time ### Environment - OS: CentOS 7 / Linux x86_64 - OpenCode: latest (running May 2026) - Shell: bash ### Summary OpenCode generates temporary ELF shared object (`.so`) files in `/tmp` and **never cleans them up**. Over time, this accumulates into hundreds of gigabytes of disk space consumed by orphaned files. ### Reproducible Steps 1. Run OpenCode CLI for an extended period (days/weeks) 2. Observe `/tmp` directory ### Observed Behavior - OpenCode creates hidden `.so` files in `/tmp` with naming pattern: - `.5fff*-00000000.so` (4.3 MB each) - `.7bef*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - `.fbff*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - These are ELF 64-bit LSB shared objects (`file` output: "ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, not stripped") - New files are generated continuously (creation timestamps within seconds of current time) - **Old files are never deleted** — they accumulate indefinitely ### Impact On one system running OpenCode: | Metric | Before Cleanup | After Cleanup | |--------|---------------|---------------| | `/tmp` size | 728 GB | 252 MB | | `.so` file count | ~154,000 | 0 | | Disk usage | 1.8T / 1.9T (99%) | 1.1T / 1.9T (60%) | The system was running at 99% disk capacity, leaving only 30 GB free on a 1.9 TB disk. ### Root Cause Analysis Using `lsof`, confirmed that running `.opencode` processes hold these files as memory-mapped regions: ``` .opencode 15606 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7befcfab9d7f5ff9-00000000.so .opencode 27137 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7bef5fffbdff7fbf-00000000.so .opencode 72378 root mem REG ... /tmp/.5fffa7f6acff5fe7-00000000.so ... ``` This suggests OpenCode is generating JIT-compiled or dynamically-loaded shared libraries (possibly from V8 code caching or WASM compilation) but lacks any cleanup mechanism — no tmpwatch integration, no file rotation, no cleanup on process exit. ### Expected Behavior - Temporary files should be cleaned up when the process exits - Or at minimum, a bounded number of files should be retained (e.g., LRU eviction) - Or use a dedicated temp directory (e.g. `/tmp/opencode/`) that is cleaned on startup ### Workaround Added a cron job to clean old `.so` files daily: ``` 0 2 * * * find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name ".*.so" -type f -mtime +1 -delete ``` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Skills tool enumerates all discovered skills into system prompt with no upper bound
signals.text: ## Problem The `skill` tool injects **all** discovered skills into the system prompt via the `<available_skills>` XML block. There is no truncation, pagination, or hard cap. Every skill with a `description` is included on every turn. With a large skill library (e.g. 100 000 skills), this adds megabytes of prompt text before the user even sends a message, guaranteeing a context-window overflow. ## Prior art Issue #7269 fixed the same problem for **subagents** by adding: - `hidden: true` to hide agents from the autocomplete / prompt - `permission.task` to filter which subagents appear in the Task tool description Skills currently have no equivalent protection. ## Current behavior From the source, the skill tool description enumerates every discovered skill: ```xml <available_skills> <skill> <name>...</name> <description>...</description> <location>...</location> </skill> <!-- repeats for N skills --> </available_skills> ``` There is no limit on `N`. ## Desired behavior At minimum, one of: 1. A `hidden: true` (or `disable-model-invocation: true`) frontmatter field for SKILL.md that removes the skill from `<available_skills>` while still allowing manual invocation (e.g. `/skill-name` or `skill({ name: "..." })`). 2. A config-level `max_skills_in_prompt` cap that truncates or paginates the list. 3. Lazy loading: only show skill names, with a separate `skill list` or `skill describe <name>` lookup for descriptions. Option 1 is the most flexible and mirrors the subagent fix in #4773. ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.15.10 - Use case: large shared skill libraries (company-wide or personal vaults with 1000+ skills) - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

signals.title: session/processor: text/reasoning delta accumulation is O(N²); long agent loops hang at 50-80 turns
signals.text: ### Description When I ran opencode in headless batch mode (`opencode run --format json`) against MiniMax-M2.7 on a long-horizon agent loop, runs that went past ~50 turns started slowing down dramatically per step, eventually hanging at the 2-hour wall-clock cap I had set. I expected per-step time to stay roughly flat, but it was growing: 6s → 30s → 60s → 100s+ per step as the session got longer. When I attached `perf record` to the running bun process I saw something weird: - `__memmove_avx_unaligned_erms` in libc.so.6 was 30.27% of CPU samples - All 7 JSC `HeapHelper` GC threads were pinned at ~4% CPU each (normally idle) - Main JS thread at 85% CPU, state R, but no syscalls — pure userspace burn - All Bun Pool and HTTP Client threads idle at 0% That `__memmove` pattern is the giveaway for V8/JSC rope-flattening on `str += chunk`. I tracked it down to two spots in `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts`: - `reasoning-delta` case: `ctx.reasoningMap[value.id].text += value.text` - `text-delta` case: `ctx.currentText.text += value.text` The issue is that anything reading `.text` between writes (the UI render loop, the NDJSON serializer, the bus event broadcaster) forces V8/JSC to flatten the rope. Then the next `+=` re-copies all the prior text — O(N²) in cumulative length per part. For thinking-mode models emitting 1500+ small reasoning tokens per turn, this destroys the agent loop after enough turns accumulate. This is the same shape as the bug that was fixed in `@ai-sdk/mcp` in vercel/ai#14619 and that I just landed for vercel/ai#15669 in `processUIMessageStream` + `DefaultStreamTextResult`. But opencode's processor has its own second copy of the pattern, so even with the AI SDK fix, opencode still hangs. The bug is **not** the same as #25094. That issue is about the TUI not showing a "thinking…" indicator during long reasoning blocks (a UX/visibility issue) and is observed in interactive sessions. This issue is an algorithmic O(N²) in the processor that affects every mode of opencode — headless batch, TUI, server — and is independent of whether thinking is shown to the user. Distinct from related issues I checked: - #17516 (opencode run hangs after completing tool calls) — describes a different symptom - #13841 (subagent hangs indefinitely, no timeout or recovery) — about subagent recovery - #5361 (TUI freezes periodically) — TUI-specific Effect when patched (with the matching vercel/ai#15669 fix applied as well): | Run config | per-step (avg) | 2h timeouts | |---|---:|---:| | unpatched | 61 s | 5 of 18 (28%) | | patched | 21 s | 0 of 53 | ### Plugins `@tabnine/tabnine-provider` (Tabnine LLM gateway provider). The bug reproduces regardless of provider — same pattern hit on local vLLM, OpenRouter, and Anthropic direct. ### OpenCode version 1.15.11 (also confirmed on 1.15.12 install path) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a long agent loop with a thinking-mode model that emits many small reasoning deltas (MiniMax M2.x, DeepSeek-V4-thinking, Kimi K2, GPT-o, Qwen3-thinking — Claude extended-thinking is less severe but also affected) 2. Drive it through 50+ turns (SWE-bench batch eval is an easy way to hit this naturally) 3. Watch per-step latency grow within the run 4. Attach `perf record -F 99 -g -p <bun_pid> -- sleep 60` to a hung process and you'll see `__memmove_avx_unaligned_erms` dominating ### Operating system Debian 12 (in container; symptom reproduces on host too) ### Terminal Headless — `opencode run --format json` invoked from a Python batch runner. Symptom does not require a TUI.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Auto-discover skills from nested subdirectories (downward walk)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Today, OpenCode's project-local skill discovery only walks **up** from the current working directory to the git worktree root. I'd like discovery to also walk **down**: when the agent is working on a file inside a subdirectory, it should pick up skills defined in that subdirectory's own skill folders. This is the standard monorepo use-case where each package ships its own skills. Another use-case it is useful for is when spawning the agent in the root of a multi-repo folder. #### Concrete example ``` ~/work/ # workspace root, where I start opencode ├── repo-a/ # separate git repo │ ├── .opencode/skills/ │ │ └── repo-a-conventions/SKILL.md # want this loaded when working in repo-a │ └── src/... ├── repo-b/ # separate git repo │ ├── .opencode/skills/ │ │ └── repo-b-deploy/SKILL.md # want this loaded when working in repo-b │ └── src/... └── repo-c/ ├── .claude/skills/ │ └── repo-c-style/SKILL.md # Claude-compatible path, same expectation └── src/... ``` **Expected:** while the agent operates on files in `repo-a/`, the `repo-a-conventions` skill is available; in `repo-b/`, `repo-b-deploy` is available; and so on. Each repository's skills load when work happens inside that repository. **Actual:** only skills on the upward path from the start directory are discovered, and discovery stops at a single git worktree. Sibling repositories' skill folders below the start dir are never loaded. Tested on OpenCode `1.15.7`. #### Prior art / context - This was previously raised in #10964 ("Auto-discovery of nested skills"), which is now closed. - Claude Code has supported this since [v2.1.6](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.6#:~:text=Added%20automatic%20discovery%20of%20skills%20from%20nested%20.claude/skills%20directories%20when%20working%20with%20files%20in%20subdirectories) #### Possible acceptance criteria - Skills are discovered from `.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, and `.agents/skills/` in subdirectories **below** the start directory, scoped to the repo/dir the agent is currently operating in. - Discovery is not limited to a single git worktree: sibling repositories inside the workspace are each eligible. - A given repository's skills load when the agent works within that repository (lazy/on-demand is fine). - Reasonable handling of name collisions across repos (e.g. nearest/active repo wins, or namespace by repo), whatever matches any OpenCode precedence. Note: this would also cover the monorepo case (packages with their own skills) via the same mechanism.

signals.title: MiniMax direct API caching may be broken or affected by new thinking toggle, while OpenRouter BYOK still caches correctly
signals.text: ### Description I noticed a possible regression with MiniMax M3 when using the direct MiniMax API token plan in opencode. Until today around noon, caching with the direct MiniMax token plan API worked correctly for me in opencode. The 5h usage limit decreased much more slowly when repeated context was cached. After the recent opencode update that added the MiniMax thinking toggle with the options default, none, and thinking, the direct MiniMax API path seems to burn through the token plan quota much faster. It looks like cached tokens are either not being counted correctly, not being reported correctly, or not being discounted against the MiniMax token plan quota. The important part: the same workflow still appears to cache correctly when using OpenRouter BYOK with MiniMax in opencode. The thinking toggle is only visible for the direct MiniMax API provider, not for OpenRouter BYOK. Environment OS: Windows 11 opencode version: please insert current version Provider affected: MiniMax direct API Model: MiniMax M3 Plan: MiniMax token plan API Alternative provider tested: OpenRouter BYOK with MiniMax Thinking setting shown only on MiniMax direct API: default, none, thinking What changed Before today: MiniMax direct API token plan worked normally in opencode Prompt caching seemed to reduce quota usage correctly Long coding sessions were possible without burning through the 5h usage limit too quickly After the update: MiniMax direct API token plan burns through the 5h limit much faster Cache does not seem to reduce quota usage as before This started around the same time the MiniMax thinking toggle appeared in opencode OpenRouter BYOK with MiniMax still appears to cache correctly Expected behavior When using MiniMax direct API with MiniMax M3, repeated context should benefit from prompt caching as before. If thinking is set to default, it should not unexpectedly change caching behavior or cause much faster quota usage. If the thinking toggle changes the request body or disables/affects caching, this should be visible or documented. Actual behavior MiniMax direct API appears to consume the token plan quota much faster than before. It feels like cached context is no longer reducing usage properly, or the new thinking toggle changes the MiniMax direct API request in a way that affects caching or token-plan accounting. OpenRouter BYOK with the same MiniMax model still behaves normally and appears to cache correctly. Steps to reproduce 1. Configure opencode with MiniMax direct API token plan. 2. Use MiniMax M3. 3. Leave the new thinking toggle on default. 4. Run an agentic coding workflow with repeated context. 5. Observe MiniMax token plan 5h usage. 6. Run the same or similar workflow through OpenRouter BYOK with MiniMax. 7. Compare cache behavior and quota consumption. Additional test suggestion It would be useful to compare the raw request body sent by opencode before and after the MiniMax thinking toggle change. Especially check whether opencode now sends a new parameter for MiniMax direct API when thinking is set to default. signals.title: `opencode web` shows `ENOENT: xdg-open` error in container environments
signals.text: ## Description Running `opencode web` inside a container (Docker/Podman) without a desktop environment prints an ugly `ENOENT` error because `xdg-open` is not present in the image. The full error: ``` 662 | var file = this.spawnfile = options.file, spawnargs; 663 | if (options.args === @undefined) 664 | spawnargs = this.spawnargs = []; 665 | else 666 | validateArray(options.args, "options.args"), spawnargs = this.spawnargs = options.args; 667 | if (this.#handle = Bun.spawn({ Error: Executable not found in $PATH: "xdg-open" path: "xdg-open", errno: -2, syscall: "spawn xdg-open", code: "ENOENT" at spawn (node:child_process:667:35) at spawn (node:child_process:14:39) at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-8mgmcy90.js:3:5152) ``` ### Update (1.17.3) Since **1.17.3** the HTTP server **does start** even when `xdg-open` is missing — the crash in 1.17.1 was fixed on 1.17.3. However, the error is still printed to stderr on startup, which is noisy and confusing for users running in containers. The error has no useful meaning in a container environment: there is no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, and no browser to open. The server works fine, but the user sees a scary stack trace before any output. ## Root cause When `opencode web` starts, it spawns `xdg-open` to open the user's default browser. In a container environment (no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, no `xdg-utils` installed), this call fails with `ENOENT`. In 1.17.1 the exception killed the entire process. In 1.17.3 the crash is fixed, but the error is still logged to stderr before the server starts. The server and the browser-opening logic should be decoupled: a missing or failed browser launch should be silent (or at most a warning) in headless environments. ## Why this matters ### 1. Containers are a first-class deployment target OpenCode's own install page documents `docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode` as an official installation method. Containers are also used for: - **CI/CD pipelines** — running opencode in automated workflows - **Remote development** — SSH into a host that runs opencode in a container, access the web UI from the browser on the local machine - **Multi-tenant setups** — isolating projects in separate containers on the same host - **Development environments** — using Dev Containers, Podman, or Docker Compose for reproducible workspaces In all these scenarios, the browser runs on the *host*, not inside the container. The container should only serve the web UI; the user opens it manually from their host browser. ### 2. The web server and the browser launch are separate concerns `opencode web` serves an HTTP interface. Opening a browser is a convenience feature for local desktop usage, but it should not be a hard requirement for the server to start. In headless or containerized contexts, this convenience becomes a blocker. ### 3. No graceful fallback exists There is currently no flag like `--no-open` or `--no-browser` to skip the browser launch. The environment variable `BROWSER` is not checked. The only workaround is either: - Installing `xdg-utils` inside the container (pointless — there is no browser to open) - Creating a fake `/usr/local/bin/xdg-open` no-op script (as done in `Containerfile` in this directory) Neither is a proper solution. ## Suggested fix The browser launch error should be suppressed or downgraded to a debug-level log when `xdg-open` is not found: ```typescript try { spawn('xdg-open', [url]); } catch (err) { // Container/headless environment — not an error } ``` Additionally, consider adding: - A `--no-open` / `--no-browser` CLI flag for `opencode web` - Support for the `BROWSER` environment variable as an alternative to `xdg-open` - A `server.openBrowser` config option in `opencode.json` (default: `true`) ## Workaround (immediate) When you create a custom container and add the standard installation method: Add this to your Containerfile before the `ENTRYPOINT`: ```dockerfile # Create a fake xdg-open RUN printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > /usr/local/bin/xdg-open && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/xdg-open ``` This creates a no-op `xdg-open` that satisfies the executable check without actually trying to open a browser. ## Environment - **OpenCode version:** 1.17.1+ (error persists in 1.17.3, though the crash was fixed) - **OS:** Any Linux container (Debian, Alpine, etc.) - **Runtime:** Docker, Podman, or any OCI-compatible container runtime ### Plugins standard opencode plugin as it comes from the factory ### OpenCode version 1.17.3 but from 1.17.1 exist the issue ### Steps to reproduce Simply pull the standard image: podman pull ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:1.17.3 and run with the web parameter and the error will be displayed on the screen. But this is my Containerfile ```dockerfile FROM docker.io/debian:stable-backports ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive ENV PIP_USER=true # Pre-configurar tshark para que no requiera setuid (ejecutamos como root en el contenedor) RUN echo "wireshark-common wireshark-common/install-setuid boolean false" | debconf-set-selections # Instalar todas las herramientas: esenciales, build, python, red y utilidades varias RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ ca-certificates \ curl \ git \ jq \ bash \ file \ unzip \ zip \ gcc \ g++ \ make \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # Crear la estructura de directorios usada por opencode.sh para XDG y PYTHONUSERBASE RUN mkdir -p /home/opencode/.config \ /home/opencode/.local/state \ /home/opencode/.local/share \ /home/opencode/.pythonuser # Instalar opencode mediante el instalador oficial RUN curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash \ && ln -sf /root/.opencode/bin/opencode /usr/local/bin/opencode # Copiar y preparar el entrypoint que decide entre modo web y TUI COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh # Base para paquetes Python instalados por el usuario (persistente mediante volumen) ENV PYTHONUSERBASE=/home/opencode/.pythonuser # Directorio de trabajo por defecto: coincide con el volumen montado en opencode.sh WORKDIR /workspace # Puerto por defecto del servidor web de opencode EXPOSE 4096 # Por defecto se arranca el servidor web en 0.0.0.0:4096. # El modo TUI se activa con OPENCODE_MODE=tui (lo hace opencode.sh con --tui/--no-web). ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh"] CMD ["web", "--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"] ``` Entrypoint.sh ```shell #!/bin/bash set -e # opencode container entrypoint. # El modo se selecciona mediante la variable de entorno OPENCODE_MODE: # - web (por defecto): ejecuta `opencode` con los argumentos recibidos # (típicamente los del CMD: web --port N --hostname ...) # - tui: ejecuta `opencode` sin argumentos (arranca la TUI) MODE="${OPENCODE_MODE:-web}" case "$MODE" in tui) exec opencode ;; web) exec opencode "$@" ;; *) echo "[ERROR] OPENCODE_MODE desconocido: '$MODE' (valores válidos: 'web', 'tui')" >&2 exit 1 ;; esac ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link ▄ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀▄ █▀▀▀ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ Local access: http://localhost:4097 Network access: http://192.168.0.113:4097 662 | var file = this.spawnfile = options.file, spawnargs; 663 | if (options.args === @undefined) 664 | spawnargs = this.spawnargs = []; 665 | else 666 | validateArray(options.args, "options.args"), spawnargs = this.spawnargs = options.args; 667 | if (this.#handle = Bun.spawn({ ^ error: Executable not found in $PATH: "xdg-open" path: "xdg-open", errno: -2, syscall: "spawn xdg-open", spawnargs: [ "http://localhost:4097" ], code: "ENOENT" at spawn (node:child_process:667:35) at spawn (node:child_process:14:39) at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-j1dejnx8.js:3:5152) ### Operating System Host Debian 13 , podman 5.4.2, inside the container: docker.io/debian:stable-backports ### Terminal terminator but this not matter

signals.title: Bash tool hangs until timeout on Windows when spawned process keeps a stdout/stderr pipe open (dev servers, daemons)
signals.text: ### Description On Windows, the `bash` tool blocks until its timeout fires even though the requested command has effectively completed, whenever a spawned child/grandchild process stays alive **and** keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe open (e.g. `vite`, `uvicorn`, `npm run dev`). The tool waits for the stdout stream collector to terminate (pipe EOF), not just for the process to exit — so a long-lived process that holds the pipe write end means the call never resolves on its own. This appears to be the still-unfixed tail of a known chain: - #20902 — bash hangs when a command spawns background child processes (`close` vs `exit`). - #22012 — explicitly notes PR #20901 (v1.3.14) only fixed background processes that produce **no** output; continuously-outputting ones (uvicorn / npm run dev / docker compose up) still hang because the stdout stream collector never terminates. - #24784 — Windows-specific: grandchild inherits the stdout pipe handle, keeping the pipe open after the direct child exits. Filing this as a focused, reproducible **Windows + PowerShell** data point on top of those, since the existing reports are mostly Linux/WSL/bash framed and one of them (#24784) has no repro upvotes yet. ### What I observed (empirical, Windows 11 + PowerShell 5.1) Starting the same dev servers three different ways gives three different outcomes — the differentiator is purely **who holds the stdout/stderr pipe**: | Launch method | stdout/stderr destination | bash tool behavior | |---|---|---| | `node start.mjs` where the script does `spawn(cmd, args, { stdio: 'inherit' })` to start Vite | inherits the bash pipe | **Hangs to timeout** (Vite is long-lived → pipe never EOFs). Confirmed: call ended with `shell tool terminated command after exceeding timeout 60000 ms`, and the port was not actually LISTENing afterward. | | `Start-Process powershell ... -WindowStyle Hidden -RedirectStandardOutput out.log -RedirectStandardError err.log -PassThru` | redirected to files (not the bash pipe) | **Returns in <1s**, prints the wrapper PID. No hang. | | `run_in_background=true` on a dev server | inherits the bash pipe | Still never "completes" because the daemon never exits — background mode also waits on process end. | So on Windows the only reliable way to launch a persistent dev server without hanging the tool is to detach via `Start-Process` and redirect stdio to files, getting the pipe out of the loop entirely. ### Minimal reproduction (PowerShell) ```powershell # Hangs the bash tool until timeout: child keeps writing to the inherited stdout pipe powershell -Command "npm.cmd run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 28000" # Returns immediately: stdout/stderr redirected to files, pipe is never held by the daemon Start-Process powershell -ArgumentList '-NoProfile','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-Command','npm.cmd run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 28000' -WindowStyle Hidden -RedirectStandardOutput out.log -RedirectStandardError err.log -PassThru ``` (Equivalent with `python -m uvicorn app:app --port 8765` in place of the npm command.) ### Expected vs actual - **Expected:** once the foreground command's own work is done (or for a daemon, once it has started), the tool should resolve based on process `exit` rather than blocking on stream/pipe EOF held by a surviving child. - **Actual:** the tool stays `running` until the timeout kills it, because the stdout stream collector waits for the pipe write end to close, which a long-lived child never does. ### Suggested direction (matching #22012 / #20902 discussion) Don't gate completion on the stdout/stderr stream collector finishing. Resolve on process `exit` and stop reading the pipe shortly after exit (e.g. a short grace window post-`exit`), so a surviving grandchild holding the pipe can't keep the tool execution promise pending. This generalizes the partial `close`→`exit` fix from PR #20901 to the continuously-outputting case. ### Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Shell: Windows PowerShell 5.1 - Node: v25.2.1, npm 11.6.2 - Python: 3.11.7 (uvicorn case) - Frameworks reproduced with: Vite 5.4 (`npm run dev`), FastAPI/uvicorn 0.32 ### Related - #20902 - #22012 - #24784 - PR #20901

signals.title: [FEATURE]:[Feature Request] Native background session autosaver / crash recovery mechanism
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Yes. Currently, if OpenCode is closed abruptly (e.g., clicking the 'X' on a terminal window, a sudden power failure, or a system crash), the active session history, chat logs, and UI layout are entirely wiped or corrupted. Because the SQLite DB (`opencode.db`) and localized session JSONs fall out of sync on sudden exit, the next launch results in a completely blank session slate. Relying purely on `/exit` for a graceful flush is highly fragile for long developer sessions. ### Describe the solution you'd like I would love to see a native, internal **Autosaver/Guardian** mechanism built into the OpenCode background server architecture. - It could periodically snapshot or flush the current terminal state, database caches, and session history into a temporary delta file or backup directory at a set interval (e.g., every 30 or 60 seconds). - If OpenCode launches and detects a previously non-graceful shutdown, it should prompt the user: *"We detected an unsaved session from [Timestamp]. Would you like to restore it?"* or seamlessly recover it. ### Describe alternatives you've considered Currently, I have to run a custom python background script daemon that watches `~/.cache/opencode` every 30 seconds and manually copies snapshots to a backup directory, paired with a recovery script to paste them back if a crash happens. While this works, a native internal solution would be significantly more robust and benefit the entire community. ### Additional context This would dramatically reduce developer anxiety surrounding crashes or accidental terminal closures during deep AI development sessions.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: local ollama support
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### **Problem** Right now, using local Ollama models with OpenCode is either undocumented, partially broken, or confusing compared to cloud-based providers (e.g. Ollama Cloud or OpenAI-compatible endpoints). Even though Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible API (`/v1/chat/completions`), OpenCode does not clearly or reliably support: * local model discovery * correct tool-calling behavior with local models * full configuration parity with cloud providers * context length configuration (`num_ctx`) * proper separation of model types (chat / vision / embedding) As a result, local-first setups are hard to use or require fragile manual configuration. --- ### **Use case** Many users want to run OpenCode fully locally using: * Ollama on `http://localhost:11434` * coder models (e.g. Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek) * optional vision models * embedding models for indexing This is important for: * privacy-focused workflows * offline development environments * GPU-limited local setups * avoiding cloud provider costs --- ### **Proposed feature** Add first-class support for **local Ollama provider mode**, similar to OpenAI-compatible providers. #### 1. Native local provider support Allow a clean config like: ```json { "provider": { "ollama": { "name": "Ollama (local)", "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/v1" } } } } ``` --- #### 2. Model auto-discovery Support fetching models from: * `/api/tags` (Ollama native) * or `/v1/models` (OpenAI-compatible layer) Then automatically classify: * chat models * vision models * embedding models --- #### 3. Explicit model type support Allow marking models explicitly: ```json "models": { "qwen2.5-coder": { "name": "Qwen Coder", "type": "chat" }, "nomic-embed": { "name": "Embeddings", "type": "embedding" }, "llava": { "name": "Vision Model", "type": "vision" } } ``` --- #### 4. Tool calling reliability improvements Ensure local Ollama models: * properly trigger tool calls (not just print JSON) * follow OpenAI tool schema consistently * are not blocked by provider abstraction differences --- ### **Expected outcome** With proper local Ollama support: * OpenCode becomes fully usable offline * tool calling works reliably with local coder models * embeddings + vision pipelines become possible locally * configuration complexity is significantly reduced --- ### **Why this matters** Right now local Ollama support feels like a “best effort integration”, while cloud providers are first-class. Making Ollama a first-class provider would significantly improve adoption for local-first users.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Reliable, reusable GUI operation
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request A model can already click around a graphical app from the raw screen, but it does it weakly — re-reading pixels every step, guessing coordinates, and re-figuring out the same app on every run. It's slow, expensive, and brittle. I'd like to make GUI operation solid. Where an app exposes an accessibility tree, the agent acts on real structure — controls, labels, values — with OCR to fill the gaps, instead of guessing from pixels: click, type, key, all through the existing permission flow. And a successful run is recorded as a reusable flow — its states, locators, actions, and the checks that confirm each step — then replayed next time instead of re-explored. When the UI shifts and a check fails, only the broken step is repaired, not the whole flow. Related to #20490, which covers the raw computer-use loop — screenshot, then inject mouse and keyboard, per OS. That's the pixel-based control this improves on: the focus here is reading structure instead of guessing coordinates, plus recording flows so a task isn't re-derived every run. The two can compose — raw input injection could sit underneath as one backend — but reliability and reuse are the point. I have a working implementation. I'd rather agree on the shape here before a PR: how it surfaces as tools, where recorded flows live relative to skills, and the permission model for actions.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: LSP opt-in whitelist mode — replace blacklist with enabled array
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. I have verified this feature hasn't been suggested before. ### Current behavior The current LSP configuration uses an **opt-out (blacklist)** model: ```jsonc { "lsp": { "zls": { "disabled": true }, "tinymist": { "disabled": true }, "texlab": { "disabled": true }, // ... 20+ lines to disable unused LSPs "biome": { "disabled": true }, "astro": { "disabled": true } } } ``` Problems: 1. Low transparency — users don't know which LSPs are enabled by default. 2. Verbose config — must disable 20+ LSPs even if only using 2-3 languages. 3. Counter-intuitive — listing what you don't want is backwards. ### Proposed solution Introduce an **opt-in (whitelist)** mode using an `enabled` array: ```jsonc { "lsp": { "enabled": [ "typescript-language-server", "biome", "pyright", "rust-analyzer" ] } } ``` Benefits: 1. Simpler config — only list LSPs you use (3-5 entries vs 20+ disabled). 2. Full transparency — config explicitly shows active LSPs. 3. Future-proof — new LSPs don't affect you unless added to whitelist. 4. Resource efficient — no unused LSP processes consuming memory. The existing `disabled` blacklist mode should still be supported for backward compatibility. When `enabled` is present, only listed LSPs start; when absent, current default-all behavior applies. ### Additional context Useful for: - Resource-constrained machines - Users working with only 1-2 languages - CI/headless environments

signals.title: Type safety loss in Copilot chat chunks and inline process.env writes in provider
signals.text: ### Description Two type-safety and code-hygiene issues in the core and opencode packages: 1. **Copilot chat chunk type safety loss** (`packages/core/src/github-copilot/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts`): The data chunk schema was inlined as an anonymous generic parameter, causing the `ChunkValue` type inference to be lost downstream. A `MUST FIX` TODO marked this. Extracting the schema as a named const (`OpenAICompatibleChatChunkDataSchema`) and adding an explicit `ChunkValue` type restores type safety. 2. **process.env direct writes** (`packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`): AWS Bedrock and SAP AI Core SDKs read from the real `process.env`, which Effect's `Env.set` does not propagate to. The code wrote directly to `process.env` with inline TODOs. A `setEnvToken()` helper centralizes this workaround and removes the TODOs. ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version dev (latest) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Inspect `openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts` — chunk value type is `unknown` due to generic schema parameter 2. Inspect `provider.ts` — `process.env[key] = token` appears inline with TODO comments ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal N/A

signals.title: Code hygiene: duplicate formatter logic, redundant array passes, and wrongly skipped tests
signals.text: ### Description Three code-hygiene issues in the opencode package: 1. **Duplicate formatter logic** (`packages/opencode/src/format/formatter.ts`, `index.ts`): Ruff and uv formatters have separate enable/disable logic. uv fallback can be merged into `ruff.enabled()`, and the special-case linked-disable code in `index.ts` can be eliminated. 2. **Unnecessary array passes in `normalizeMessages`** (`packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts`): The Anthropic/Bedrock path runs sanitize, then filter, then a second filter — three array allocations. Fusing sanitize + empty-filter into a single for-loop reduces this to one pass. 3. **Skipped tests in session-message-updater** (`packages/opencode/test/v2/session-message-updater.test.ts`): Three tests are marked `test.skip` but the implementation behavior is correct — the test expectations were wrong. Fixing the expectations and unskipping restores coverage. ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version dev (latest) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Inspect `format/formatter.ts` — uv and ruff have parallel logic that can be shared 2. Inspect `provider/transform.ts` — `normalizeMessages` does 3 separate `.map()/.filter()` passes 3. Run `bun test test/v2/session-message-updater.test.ts` — 3 tests show as skipped ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal N/A

The same LazyCodex/OmO installation works correctly in the OpenCode VS Code extension and when running OpenCode directly inside WSL. The prompt after the error appears is: ```js convertSDKMessageToStoredMessage(message), createdAt: message.info?.time?.created ?? Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, id: typeof message.id === "string" ? message.id : "" }))', 'messages.map' is undefined) ``` ### Plugins opencode-pty, opencode-kimi-full, @warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp, oh-my-openagent@latest ### OpenCode version 1.17.8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install the following plugins in opencode in WSL: - opencode-pty - opencode-kimi-full - @warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp - oh-my-openagent@latest 2. Connect opencode in WSL via the OpenCode beta Windows desktop client. 3. Open a workspace that is hosted in WSL (remote connection). 4. signals.title: Unbounded growth of the `event` table: opencode.db reaches 13GB+, mostly `message.updated.1` snapshots (no retention/compaction)
signals.text: ## Summary The local SQLite store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) grows **unbounded** on long-lived instances because the event-sourcing `event` table is never pruned, capped, or compacted. On two of our long-running instances it reached **~13 GB each**, filling a 22 GB volume to 97–99% and eventually producing `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` on ordinary queries — the instance becomes effectively unusable. The actual conversation data is tiny by comparison; **>90% of the DB is the event log**, and within it a single event type (`message.updated.1`) dominates. ## Measured breakdown (real instance, 13.7 GB DB) ``` page_size=4096 page_count=3342166 total=13.69 GB freelist_count=18 dead=0.00 GB (0.0%) <- live data, VACUUM does not help ``` Per-table (`sum(length(data))`): | table | rows | size | avg/row | |---------|---------|-----------|---------| | **event** | 141,951 | **12.20 GB** | 83.9 KB | | message | 6,955 | 1.15 GB | 161 KB | | part | 27,775 | 0.07 GB | 2.4 KB | | others | — | ~0 | — | Within `event`, by `type`: | event type | rows | size | avg | |-------------------------------|--------|------------|---------| | **`message.updated.1`** | 26,463 | **11.94 GB** | **440 KB** | | `session.next.tool.success.1` | 7,843 | 0.12 GB | 14.8 KB | | `message.part.updated.1` | 52,644 | 0.10 GB | 1.8 KB | | everything else | ~55k | < 0.3 GB | — | So ~87% of the entire database is `message.updated.1` events. With ~6,955 messages there are ~3.8 `message.updated` events per message, each persisting what looks like a full message snapshot (avg 440 KB), and **all historical snapshots are retained forever**. The same pattern was observed independently on a second instance (also ~13 GB, same `event`-table dominance), so this is reproducible, not a one-off. ## Root cause (confirmed in source, `dev` branch) `packages/core/src/event/sql.ts` — the `event` table has no TTL, no row cap, no size limit, and no compaction column; it just stores every event's full `data` JSON: ```ts export const EventTable = sqliteTable("event", { id: text().$type<EventV2.ID>().primaryKey(), aggregate_id: text().notNull().references(() => EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, { onDelete: "cascade" }), seq: integer().notNull(), type: text().notNull(), data: text({ mode: "json" }).$type<Record<string, unknown>>().notNull(), }, ...) ``` `packages/core/src/event.ts` — the **only** delete against `event` is a full-aggregate cascade, used when an entire session/aggregate is removed: ```ts function remove(aggregateID: string) { return db.transaction(() => Effect.gen(function* () { yield* db.delete(EventSequenceTable).where(eq(EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() yield* db.delete(EventTable).where(eq(EventTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() })).pipe(Effect.orDie) } ``` There is **no partial pruning** — nothing collapses superseded `message.updated.*` snapshots, keeps only the latest per message, caps per-aggregate history, or stores deltas. `packages/opencode/src/sync/README.md` confirms this is an intentional append-only log "for session replayability." That's a reasonable design goal, but with full-snapshot `message.updated` events and no retention it means every session's event history accumulates for the lifetime of the session, with no upper bound. `SessionCompaction.prune` does **not** address this — it trims context tokens sent to the model, not persisted `event` rows. ## Impact - Disk exhaustion on long-lived instances (containers/sandboxes/servers with persistent home dirs). - Once the volume is full, even read queries that need temp space fail with `database or disk is full`. - `VACUUM` cannot reclaim it (freelist ≈ 0%; it is all live data). The only current remediation is deleting whole sessions (cascade) or manually `DELETE FROM event ...`. ## Suggested fixes (any one would help) 1. **Compact superseded snapshots**: for snapshot-style events like `message.updated.*`, retain only the latest event per `(aggregate_id, message_id)` (or per message `seq`), deleting older ones — newer fully supersedes older. 2. **Store deltas instead of full snapshots** for `message.updated` (the README already notes `session.updated` was moved to fields-only; `message.updated` appears to still carry a full snapshot). 3. **Per-aggregate retention cap / periodic compaction** of the event log for inactive/completed sessions. ## Environment - Observed on builds in the 1.15.x–1.17.x range; root cause confirmed present on `dev` (current `latest`, 1.17.9) via the source above. - SQLite store at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Happy to provide the full per-session breakdown or a repro script if useful.

signals.title: False positive content-filter on claude-fable-5 — charged ~$20 for blocked output
signals.text: ## Summary `claude-fable-5` model responses to benign queries are being blocked by opencode's `content-filter` guardrail. The cache write is billed (~$6.69 each) despite the filter preventing any output from reaching the user. Total charged for blocked outputs: **~$20** ## Evidence All 3 calls were killed by content-filter with only 1-5 output tokens produced: | Time | Tokens | Output | Cost | Filter | |---|---|---|---|---| | Call 1 | 534,929 | 1 | $6.69 | content-filter | | Call 2 | 534,963 | 1 | $6.69 | content-filter | | Call 3 | 534,982 | 5 | $6.69 | content-filter | | **Total** | | | **$20.06** | | From opencode's SQLite DB — each assistant response shows: ``` step-start → {"reason":"content-filter","type":"step-finish"} ``` ## Problems 1. Content filter is generating **false positives** — blocking clearly benign queries. 2. **Cache writes are billed at full price** even when opencode's own guardrail kills the output. 3. User receives **zero output** but pays full cache write cost. 4. **No notification** that output was filtered — just appears as empty response. ## Request Refund for the ~$20 in blocked calls and investigate why content-filter is triggering on benign queries.
