signal.title: bug(session): infinite compaction loop when compression fails to reduce context
signal.text: ## Bug Description The session loop in `prompt.ts` can enter an infinite compaction loop: ``` overflow detected → compact → still overflow → compact → ... (infinite) ``` This happens when compaction fails to reduce the context below the token limit — for example, when compression state is lost, messages are inherently uncompressable, or the compression plugin returns an error. The loop spins indefinitely consuming API credits without making progress. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Have a session with large context that triggers overflow 2. If compaction fails or doesn't reduce tokens enough, the loop retries indefinitely 3. Observe continuous API calls with no progress ## Root Cause The `runLoop` function has two paths that trigger compaction and `continue` without any guard: 1. **Overflow check**: after each step, if `compaction.isOverflow()` returns true, it calls `compaction.create()` and continues — but the next iteration sees the same overflow and repeats. 2. **Compact result**: when the provider returns `"compact"` as the result, it calls `compaction.create()` and continues — same infinite loop if compaction doesn't actually reduce context. Neither path has a retry counter or break condition. ## Expected Behavior After a reasonable number of compaction attempts (e.g., 2), the loop should break and return an error to the user, rather than spinning indefinitely.
signal.author: ranxianglei

signal.title: v2 plugin: tool input decode breaks when server effect version drifts from plugin's effect
signal.text: ## Summary Plugin-provided tools are silently version-coupled to the server's bundled `effect`. When the managed service auto-updated to a build bundling `effect@4.0.0-beta.107`, every tool from a config plugin built against `effect@4.0.0-beta.101` began failing input decode with `Invalid tool input: Expected object` — input-independent, for every tool, until the plugin's `effect` is manually realigned with the server bundle. Any server update that bumps `effect` can break all installed effect plugins. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-beta-17595 (managed service, auto-updated mid-session from an earlier beta) - OS: Darwin 25.5.0 (darwin arm64) - Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty) - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: beta - Active plugins: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/session-control.ts` (effect plugin; the one affected), opencode-voice agent plugin, debug-workspace-plugin ## Reproduction 1. Install a config plugin that defines tools via `@opencode-ai/plugin/effect` with `Schema.Struct` input schemas, with `effect@4.0.0-beta.101` in the config directory's `node_modules` (`~/.config/opencode/package.json` pinning `effect: 4.0.0-beta.101`). 2. Run a server build bundling `effect@4.0.0-beta.107` (e.g. current beta `0.0.0-beta-17595`). 3. From Code Mode, call any of the plugin's tools with a perfectly valid input, e.g. `tools.session.get({})`. ## Expected Behavior The tool input decodes and the tool runs — or, if plugin/server effect versions are genuinely incompatible, a loud, diagnosable error at plugin load time naming the version mismatch, not a per-call decode failure that looks like caller error. ## Actual Behavior Every call to every tool from the plugin fails with: ```text Error: Invalid tool input: Expected object ``` The error is input-independent — `{}`, a fully valid object, and even a raw string all produce the identical message: ```js await tools.session.get() // "Tool 'session.get' expects exactly one input object." (codemode arg check — works) await tools.session.get({}) // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" await tools.session.rename({ title: "probe" }) // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" await tools.session.get("string") // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" (same message, wrong-type input) ``` Code Mode builtins (`search`) and MCP-backed tools are unaffected; only effect-plugin tools fail. ## Additional Context Diagnosis trail: - The error string originates in `packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts` `decodeInput`: `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(schema)(value)` — the **server's** effect decoding the **plugin's** schema object. - The Schema `TypeId` string (`"~effect/Schema/Schema"`) is identical in beta.101 and beta.107, so the foreign schema passes `Schema.isSchema` and proceeds into the host decoder, which then fails on the drifted internals (beta.101→107 includes Schema representation/identity changes, the SchemaError move, and AST transform memoization). - Timeline: the managed service auto-updated and restarted mid-day (old pid replaced ~13:12 local); the plugin and its `node_modules` were unchanged for a week. Tools worked before the restart, and all failed after — same session, same call sites. - Workaround that fixes it: `cd ~/.config/opencode && bun add effect@4.0.0-beta.107 @opencode-ai/plugin@next`, then restart the service. This must be repeated on every server update that bumps effect. Suggested directions (any one resolves the class of failure): 1. Decode plugin tool inputs through the standard-schema interface of the *plugin's own* schema (version-agnostic: the plugin's instance validates, the host only transports), instead of running the host's `decodeUnknownEffect` on a foreign schema. 2. Have `@opencode-ai/plugin` re-export `effect` (and document that plugins must import it from there), so plugins always share the server's instance. 3. At plugin load, detect an effect-instance/version mismatch between host and plugin and fail loudly with the two versions named — turning a silent per-call decode failure into an actionable load error.

signal.title: V2 AI package: audit and close critical protocol correctness gaps
signal.text: ## Summary Track correctness and parity gaps in the V2 native `@opencode-ai/ai` package by wire protocol. This is **not** a feature wishlist. It excludes citations, provider-hosted tools, and unsupported optional capabilities. Scope is critical flow integrity: normalization, ordering, streamed-state settlement, persistence/replay, request intent, terminal outcomes, transport classification, and accounting. ## Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [x] **Coalesce parallel tool results into the immediately following user turn.** V2 previously lowered `assistant[tool_use A, tool_use B]` into `user[result A]`, `user[result B]`. Completed in #41948. - [x] **Settle or fail pending streamed tool calls at `message_stop`.** Completed in #43136. ### P0 — output and continuation integrity - [ ] **Preserve Anthropic compaction blocks and deltas.** Native accepts unknown block types structurally but silently drops compaction content from output and persisted history. - [ ] **Map compaction stop reasons and retain continuation state** rather than converting them to `unknown`. ### P1 — request normalization - [ ] **Normalize thinking budgets and answer-token semantics.** Enforce minimum budget and `budget < max_tokens`; account for thinking tokens when canonical `maxTokens` represents answer budget. - [x] **Do not silently downgrade supported system updates into wrapped user text.** Completed in #43180. - [ ] **Never replay unsigned visible `thinking` blocks.** Replay valid signed/redacted Anthropic state or fail/lower locally. - [ ] **Trim/normalize final assistant prefill whitespace** where Anthropic requires it. ### P1 — stream and accounting integrity - [ ] **Validate lifecycle ordering:** require `message_start`, reject duplicate/out-of-order starts, reject events after terminal completion, and settle open fragments at EOF. - [ ] **Aggregate raw usage once at terminal completion**, including split start/delta counters and compaction/advisor/fallback iterations. Existing tracker: #40713. - [ ] **Retain response identity and stop diagnostics:** actual served model, response ID, initial content snapshot, stop/refusal details, and complete provider metadata. ## Bedrock Converse ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [x] **Coalesce parallel tool results into one immediately following Bedrock user turn.** Completed in #41780. - [x] **Normalize adjacent user/tool messages generally** so synthetic, compaction, and ordinary user content cannot violate Converse role/turn requirements. Completed in #41780. ## OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`) ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve streamed `delta.refusal`.** Native accepts the field structurally but ignores it, allowing a refusal to become an empty successful response and disappear from persisted history. ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Classify and retain truncated tool arguments correctly.** Distinguish provider truncation, transport interruption, and adapter premature finalization; never execute malformed input; add bounded safe recovery. Existing report: #36766. ### P1 — stream integrity - [ ] **Require valid terminal lifecycle state** rather than treating partial content/tool buffers as clean completion. ## OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`) ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Finalize or fail pending function calls when `response.completed` arrives without `response.output_item.done`.** Current behavior can leave a tool permanently pending. Existing deterministic report: #37159. - [ ] **Retain terminal provider diagnostics for truncated argument buffers**, including whether the stream ended normally, finish state, and bounded byte counts. Related: #36766. ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve `response.refusal.delta` and `response.refusal.done`.** Native ignores them, yields an empty successful response, and cannot replay the refusal. ### P1 — reasoning lifecycle - [ ] **Normalize overlapping reasoning fragments** instead of crashing the execution as `unknown`. Existing report: #36892. - [x] **Finalize or explicitly interrupt every open reasoning/text fragment before response completion.** Completed by shared lifecycle settlement. ## Gemini `generateContent` ### P0 — function-call integrity - [x] **Normalize omitted zero-argument call input to `{}`.** A valid `functionCall: { name: "ping" }` currently fails decoding. Completed in #43111. ### P0 — safety outcome integrity - [x] **Preserve prompt-level safety blocks (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) as a typed terminal outcome.** Candidate-less blocked prompts currently lose the safety reason and become generic incomplete-stream failures. Completed in #43070. ## Shared V2 runner/history layer ### P0 — successful execution contract - [ ] **A successful execution must contain usable text, a refusal, or completed tool work.** Token usage or a provider `stop` alone is insufficient. Existing report: #37372. - [x] **Every announced local tool call must settle exactly once before its owning step terminates.** ### P1 — persistence and replay - [ ] **Distinguish normally ended fragments from cleanup-interrupted text, reasoning, and tool input.** Existing tracker: #36874. - [x] **Do not persist interrupted raw tool input as an executable call.** ### P1 — request intent - [x] **Keep variants effective after native package overrides.** ### P1 — transport and error classification - [x] **Classify response-body resets as transport failures, not invalid model output**, and retain a sanitized low-level cause. Completed in #41779; existing report: #39326. - [x] **Before output starts, preserve bounded transport retry behavior.** After output/tool side effects begin, expose an explicit interrupted-step recovery path rather than silently retrying. - [x] **Keep child-session stream failures visible to the parent** so dropped subagent work can be restarted. ## Protocol conformance matrix Add fixtures and differential tests for every native protocol covering: 1. Single, sequential, and parallel tool calls. 2. Adjacent user/tool/synthetic/system messages. 3. Missing, duplicate, reordered, and truncated stream boundaries. 4. Pending tools/fragments at every terminal event. 5. Text, refusal, safety block, content filter, empty response, and normal stop outcomes. 6. Same-origin replay and incompatible provider/model/protocol switching. 7. Request options and model variants at the actual wire body/header boundary. 8. Split streaming usage, cache counters, executor iterations, and fallback accounting. 9. Transport reset before output, during reasoning/text, during tool input, and after tool execution. ## Suggested implementation order 1. Anthropic Messages and Bedrock parallel-result normalization. 2. Pending tool settlement across Anthropic, Responses, Chat, and Gemini. 3. Refusal, safety, and empty-success outcome invariants. 4. Replay provenance and interrupted-fragment semantics. 5. Request option/variant normalization. 6. Transport classification and usage aggregation.

signal.title: Native crash (SIGTRAP) in fff-scan thread during watcher resubscribe after scan — FileItem::write_absolute_path overflows fixed 1024-byte buffer (macOS arm64)
signal.text: ## Summary opencode crashes with a native Rust panic in the bundled `fff` file-indexer during a scan, killing the whole process with no error in `opencode.log`. - **opencode**: 1.18.18 (latest at time of filing) - **Platform**: macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon (arm64) - **Crash reports**: `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/opencode-2026-08-18-210957.ips` and `opencode-2026-08-18-222412.ips` — two crashes ~75 min apart, **byte-identical** faulting stack. ## Crash signature ``` EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP faultingThread: 33, thread name: "fff-scan" fff_search::types::FileItem::write_absolute_path::h6be4aaca40dafd85 fff_search::scan::rescubscribe_watcher_post_scan::hd9b19e5fc8d2229e fff_search::scan::ScanJob::run::hb82750f8c22d9326 std::sys::backtrace::__rust_begin_short_backtrace core::ops::function::FnOnce::call_once{{vtable.shim}} std::sys::thread::Thread::new::thread_start ``` ## What was happening Both crashes occurred during long agentic sessions in a git repo with multiple worktrees (`jot-brain`, `jot-brain-wt119`, `jot-brain-wtsec`). The app log shows the session running a rescan loop and stopping abruptly mid-step with **no error line**: ``` ...loop session.id=ses_... step=243 [trace/breakpoint trap] ← process dies here, nothing logged ``` ## Root cause hypothesis (from fff source) The panic is in `FileItem::write_absolute_path` (`fff-core/src/types.rs`), which writes `base_path + '/' + relative_path` into a **fixed-size stack buffer**: ```rust #[cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))] pub const PATH_BUF_SIZE: usize = libc::PATH_MAX as usize; // 1024 on macOS pub(crate) fn write_absolute_path<'a>(&self, arena, base_path, buf: &'a mut [u8; PATH_BUF_SIZE]) { let base_len = base.len(); buf[..base_len].copy_from_slice(base); // panics if base_len > 1024 ... buf[base_len] = std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR as u8; // panics if base_len == 1024 ... } ``` There is no bounds check. During `ScanJob::run` → `rescubscribe_watcher_post_scan` (`fff-core/src/scan.rs`), the watcher is re-subscribed to every indexed directory; any directory path ≥ `PATH_BUF_SIZE` (1024 on macOS) causes a `slice index out of range` Rust panic. Rust panics in the native lib abort the process via an `int3` trap → recorded by macOS as `EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP`, and **bypass the opencode JS logger**, so the app log just ends mid-loop with no error. The two identical `.ips` files confirm a deterministic trigger rather than two unrelated incidents. ## Related - #42557 — fff watcher / libgit2 busy-loop (same fff code area) - #32511, #35791, #37740 — fff over-indexing / watch explosion - #31682, #31747, #31701, #31850 — earlier (closed) fff scan crashes in 1.17.x ## Ask - Bounds-check the path write in `write_absolute_path` (fall back to heap `PathBuf` when `PATH_BUF_SIZE` is exceeded). - Consider raising `PATH_BUF_SIZE` / not truncating silently. Crash reports available on request.

signal.title: [Desktop] UI freezes after agent turns finish — renderer stuck in ResizeObserver loop; only force-quit + relaunch recovers
signal.text: ### Description The OpenCode Desktop app (Electron, v1.18.18) freezes: the window becomes completely unresponsive (no click/typing reaction, no rendering updates) shortly after an assistant turn finishes. The backend core loop is still alive — it finishes turns and logs normally — only the renderer UI is stuck. The only way to recover is force-quitting and relaunching the app. Happened twice within ~20 minutes (18:22–18:29 and 18:37–18:40 local time), each time ending with a forced app restart. The renderer log around both freezes is flooded with ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications, and the same errors keep occurring continuously even during normal operation (634 occurrences in the current session within 3.5 hours), so the layout loop is an ongoing condition that periodically escalates into a full freeze. Timeline (local time): - 18:21:55 – agent turn # 1 completes (exiting loop in core log); renderer floods with ResizeObserver errors; window freezes for ~7 min. - 18:29:05 – force-quit and relaunch (main.log: new app start). - 18:31:41 – agent turn # 2 completes; renderer floods again (18:31:38–18:35:31). - 18:36:53 – agent turn # 3 completes; window freezes again. - 18:40:10 – force-quit and relaunch again. Freezes stop only after restart. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version Desktop app 1.18.18 (auto-updater reports this as latest). ### Steps to reproduce Not 100% reproducible, but the pattern observed: 1. Open a large project folder (in my case a ~5 GB directory tree with ~2,400 files inside a Nutstore-synced folder on Windows 10). 2. Send a message and let the assistant turn complete. 3. Within seconds after the turn finishes, the window freezes for 3–7 minutes; input and rendering stop. The agent's own turn history keeps being written to the core log during the freeze, so only the UI is affected. 4. Force-quit and relaunch the app — the session then resumes normally. Trigger seems related to rendering completed assistant messages, possibly aggravated by a very large project tree / long messages. ### Additional context Some observations from my logs that may help diagnose: 1. **Root-cause hypothesis (renderer layout loop):** The freezes start exactly when a completed assistant message is rendered into the chat. DOM size oscillation (auto-resizing scroll container / streaming content) keeps invalidating layout faster than Chromium can deliver ResizeObserver notifications, starving the renderer's main thread. The main process stays alive and responsive (auto-update checks keep firing during the freezes); only the renderer is stuck, and a full app restart is the only recovery. The errors also appear continuously during normal operation (hundreds per session), so the layout loop is persistent and periodically escalates into a complete freeze. 2. **Possible aggravating factors:** - The project is a ~5.3 GB directory tree (~2,400 files) inside a Nutstore (坚果云 / Jianguoyun) sync folder on Windows. The sync driver adds I/O latency and file locks; a large tree makes every file-tree refresh and message render slower. - Earlier today the same app instance logged a burst of `ENOENT` errors: the file API repeatedly attempted `FileSystem.list` on a project path that no longer exists (the folder name appeared duplicated, e.g. `...\Project xxx\Project xxx`, lstat -> ENOENT). This suggests stale/mismatched workspace paths are stored in the desktop app state, which can trigger repeated tree refreshes and extra renderer work. ### Screenshot and/or share link No share link available (local session). Attached: full renderer logs of the two most recent app sessions (also referenced as attachments). - Renderer log — session 20260818T102905 (contains both freezes; app launched 18:29:05, killed 18:40:10). Path: %APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\20260818T102905\renderer.log - Renderer log — session 20260818T104010 (post-restart session, current; errors continue constantly). Path: %APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\20260818T104010\renderer.log [20260818T104010.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31208494/20260818T104010.txt) [20260818T102905.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31208493/20260818T102905.txt) ### Operating System Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045) ### Terminal N/A — OpenCode Desktop app (GUI, Electron)

signal.title: A symlink inside the workspace bypasses the external_directory permission
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary The `external_directory` boundary check compares path strings and never resolves symbolic links on Linux or macOS. A workspace that contains a symlink pointing out of the tree therefore lets the built-in file tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `read`) operate on files outside the project, with `external_directory` denied and no permission prompt. The check already resolves links on Windows, and the helper that resolves real paths already exists in the same module. Only the POSIX path is affected. This is distinct from the shell-redirection bypass filed separately: `bash` is denied throughout this report, and the escape happens through the file tools. ## Version - Reproduced on `1.18.16` and `1.18.18` (latest release at time of filing) - Linux x64 - Reproduced with two different models, `github-copilot/gpt-5-mini` and `github-copilot/gpt-5.5` ## Reproduction The realistic shape is an agent working in a checkout it did not create. Symlinks that leave the tree are ordinary in real repositories. ```bash ROOT=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$ROOT/workspace" "$ROOT/OUTSIDE" ln -s "$ROOT/OUTSIDE" "$ROOT/workspace/outbox" CONFIG='{"permission":{"external_directory":"deny","bash":"deny","write":"allow","edit":"allow"}}' OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT="$CONFIG" \ opencode run --pure --format json --dir "$ROOT/workspace" \ 'Create a file at the path outbox/escaped.txt inside this directory. Its content must be exactly the text ESCAPED with no trailing newline.' ls -l "$ROOT/OUTSIDE/escaped.txt" ``` ## Actual ```text tool=apply_patch status=completed *** Begin Patch *** Add File: outbox/escaped.txt +ESCAPED *** End Patch -rw-rw-r-- 1 user user 8 /tmp/tmp.XXXX/OUTSIDE/escaped.txt ``` The file exists outside the workspace. No `external_directory` prompt was raised at any point. For contrast, under the identical configuration, naming the same destination directly is refused: ```text *** Add File: /tmp/tmp.XXXX/OUTSIDE/escaped.txt -> status=error, no file created ``` Both forms target the same directory, with the same tool and the same configuration. The only difference is how the path is spelled, which is precisely what the boundary check inspects. ## Expected With `external_directory` denied, a write whose real destination is outside the project should trigger the same permission check regardless of whether the path reaches that destination directly or through a symbolic link inside the workspace. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts` ```ts const full = process.platform === "win32" ? FSUtil.normalizePath(target) : target if (containsPath(full, ins)) return false ``` On Windows, `FSUtil.normalizePath` calls `realpathSync.native`. On other platforms the raw target is used unchanged. `packages/opencode/src/project/instance-context.ts` ```ts export function containsPath(filepath: string, ctx: InstanceContext): boolean { if (FSUtil.contains(ctx.directory, filepath)) return true if (ctx.worktree === "/") return false return FSUtil.contains(ctx.worktree, filepath) } ``` `packages/core/src/fs-util.ts` ```ts export function contains(parent: string, child: string) { const result = relative(parent, child) return result === "" || (!isAbsolute(result) && result !== ".." && !result.startsWith(`..${sep}`)) } ``` `relative` is pure path arithmetic. `workspace/outbox/escaped.txt` is lexically inside `workspace`, so `containsPath` returns true, the prompt is skipped, and the write follows the link into a different subtree. Two details suggest this is an oversight rather than a decision: 1. `FSUtil.resolve` lives in the same file and does call `realpathSync`, but `contains` does not use it. 2. Link resolution is already considered necessary on Windows and skipped elsewhere. All four file tools route through `assertExternalDirectory`, so `read` is affected on the same terms. The boundary can therefore be crossed in both directions. ## Impact `external_directory` reads as a containment boundary, and it is what an operator relies on when pointing an agent at code they do not fully trust. A repository can carry a symlink that silently widens the agent's reach, in either direction, and the user sees no prompt because the runtime believes the destination is inside the project. Symlinks leaving the tree occur in ordinary development: `node_modules` layouts, monorepo tooling, build output directories, and dotfile checkouts all produce them without any adversarial intent. This is a fail-open design: a path that merely looks internal is treated as internal. ## Suggested fix Resolve both operands before comparing, using the helper that already exists: ```ts export function containsPath(filepath: string, ctx: InstanceContext): boolean { const target = FSUtil.resolve(filepath) if (FSUtil.contains(FSUtil.resolve(ctx.directory), target)) return true if (ctx.worktree === "/") return false return FSUtil.contains(FSUtil.resolve(ctx.worktree), target) } ``` `FSUtil.resolve` already returns the lexically resolved path when the destination does not exist yet, so creating a new file inside the project is unaffected. Failing closed matters more than failing open here. Treating an unresolvable path as external costs a prompt; treating it as internal costs containment. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: apply_patch/write/edit/read escape the external_directory boundary through an in-workspace symlink (POSIX)
signal.text: ### Bug description The `external_directory` permission boundary check compares the caller's path against the project directory **lexically** on POSIX and never resolves symbolic links. A workspace that contains a symlink pointing out of the tree therefore lets the built-in file tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `read`, `grep`) operate on files outside the project, with `external_directory` denied and no permission prompt. The check already resolves links on Windows (`FSUtil.normalizePath` uses `realpathSync.native`), and a real-path helper exists in the same module (`FSUtil.resolve`). Only the POSIX path is affected. ### Reproduction ```bash ROOT=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$ROOT/workspace" "$ROOT/OUTSIDE" ln -s "$ROOT/OUTSIDE" "$ROOT/workspace/outbox" CONFIG='{"permission":{"external_directory":"deny","bash":"deny","write":"allow","edit":"allow"}}' OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT="$CONFIG" \ opencode run --pure --format json --dir "$ROOT/workspace" \ 'Create a file at the path outbox/escaped.txt inside this directory. Its content must be exactly the text ESCAPED.' ls -l "$ROOT/OUTSIDE/escaped.txt" ``` Expected: the write outside the workspace is refused (or prompts). Actual: the file is created outside, with no `external_directory` prompt raised. Note the write is to a **not-yet-existing** leaf under a symlinked parent — `realpathSync` throws ENOENT on the missing leaf, so a naive resolve would fall back to the lexical path and still escape. The fix must resolve the deepest existing ancestor and re-append the suffix. ### Root cause `packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts:25`: ```ts const full = process.platform === "win32" ? FSUtil.normalizePath(target) : target if (containsPath(full, ins)) return false ``` On POSIX `full` is the raw target; `containsPath` then does a string-level containment check against `ctx.directory`/`ctx.worktree`, so an in-workspace symlink to an outside directory is treated as inside. ### Suggested fix Resolve the target to its real path (via a helper that handles a missing leaf) before the boundary check; keep the permission glob on the caller's lexical target so user-configured `external_directory` allow rules written against aliased paths keep matching. ### Impact Any workspace containing an out-of-tree symlink (ordinary in real checkouts, e.g. `node_modules` or build links) can silently bypass the `external_directory` deny/ask boundary through the file tools.

signal.title: [BUG] Archive action causes 4+ hours of session data loss on Windows Desktop
signal.text: ### Description When clicking the "Archive" button in OpenCode Desktop for Windows, all conversation history from the current session that hasn't been persisted to the database is permanently lost. This is a critical data loss bug. ## Impact - Severity: Critical (data loss) - Affected Users: All Windows Desktop users - Data Lost: 4+ hours of conversation history (in my case) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open OpenCode Desktop on Windows 10/11 2. Start a new conversation and chat for several hours 3. Do NOT manually save/export the conversation 4. Click the "Archive" button in the session list 5. The current session disappears from the list 6. All messages from ~17:57 to ~21:40 are permanently lost ## Expected Behavior - Archiving a session should save all pending messages to the database first - Archived sessions should be recoverable via an "Unarchive" function - Users should be warned if there are unsaved messages before archiving ## Actual Behavior - Session data in memory is NOT persisted before archiving - No confirmation dialog warns about unsaved data - No way to recover the archived session - Database shows no record of the lost conversation ## Technical Evidence ### Database Query Results Queried `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: ```sql SELECT id, slug, title, time_updated FROM session ORDER BY time_updated DESC LIMIT 10; ``` | Session ID | Title | Last Updated (Local Time) | |------------|-------|--------------------------| | ses_2adb34a58ffelj8oJzw2806lGG | GitHub 项目本地部署与启动流程 | 2026-04-03 14:49:12 | | ses_2ac431abcffefonOJboRolkgoG | 恢复归档会话记录 | 2026-04-03 14:37:59 | | ses_2ad40870affew5ZoDh95e1eu2N | T2: 禁用危险 Sandbox 参数 | 2026-04-03 13:44:49 | All sessions were last updated BEFORE 17:00, but I was actively chatting until 21:40. ### File System Analysis Checked `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session_diff/`: - All session diff files are empty (2 bytes, content: `[]`) - No session data persisted between 17:57-21:40 ### Timeline | Time | Event | |------|-------| | 14:49 | Last session saved to database | | 17:57 | Started new conversation (NOT in database) | | 21:40 | Clicked "Archive" button | | 21:40+ | 4+ hours of conversation history lost | ## Root Cause Analysis Based on source code review and database analysis: 1. Session auto-save mechanism is broken - Messages are not being persisted to the database in real-time 2. Archive action does not trigger a save - Clicking archive should flush pending messages first 3. No warning dialog - Users are not warned about unsaved data before archiving 4. No recovery mechanism - Archived sessions cannot be recovered ## Suggested Fixes ### Immediate (Critical) 1. Add confirmation dialog before archiving if there are unsaved messages 2. Force save pending messages before executing archive action 3. Add warning toast if archive is attempted with pending data ### Long-term 1. Implement proper session persistence - Auto-save messages every N seconds 2. Add unarchive functionality - Allow users to recover archived sessions 3. Add session backup - Create backup before destructive operations ## Workarounds (for users) Until this is fixed, users should: 1. Regularly export conversations using `/export` command (Ctrl+X X) 2. Avoid clicking "Archive" button until the bug is fixed 3. Use TUI version (`opencode` command) - community PR #13961 adds archive/unarchive support ## Related Issues - #15980 - 希望添加「恢复归档会话」的功能 - #15677 - 误操作点到归档了，如何能回撤这个操作 - #12888 - 当一个对话被"归档"，要去哪里找回它 - #16000 - [FEATURE]: Unarchive session ## Related PRs - #13961 - feat: add session archive/unarchive support to TUI - #16212 - feat(session): add archive undo + unarchive command ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal OpenCode Desktop App

signal.title: fix(tool): resolve symlinks before external_directory boundary check
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43346 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? The `external_directory` permission boundary check compared the caller's path against the project directory lexically on POSIX and never resolved symbolic links. A workspace containing a symlink that points out of the tree therefore let the built-in file tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `read`, `grep`) operate on files outside the project, with `external_directory` denied and no permission prompt. Windows already resolved links (`FSUtil.normalizePath` uses `realpathSync.native`); only the POSIX path was affected. Changes: - **`packages/core/src/fs-util.ts`**: add `FSUtil.resolveExisting`, which resolves a path to its real (symlink-resolved) form even when the final component does not exist yet. `realpathSync` throws ENOENT as soon as any component is missing, so for a not-yet-created file (the `write`/`apply_patch` case) it resolves the deepest existing ancestor and re-appends the remaining suffix. - **`packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts`**: resolve the target via `resolveExisting` before the boundary check. The permission glob still uses the caller's lexical target so user-configured `external_directory` allow rules written against aliased paths keep matching. Why it works: the boundary decision now uses the canonical real path, so an in-workspace symlink to an outside directory is correctly detected as outside; the permission glob keeps matching user rules on the paths an agent actually refers to. ### How did you verify your code works? - New regression tests in `test/tool/external-directory.test.ts` (POSIX-only): an in-workspace symlink pointing outside now raises an `external_directory` prompt both when the leaf exists and when it does not exist yet. Both failed before the fix (no prompt) and pass after. - `bun test test/tool/` : 340 pass, 0 fail (including the existing "does not ask for external_directory when alias path is allowed" test, which still passes because the glob keeps the lexical alias path). - `bun run typecheck` clean in both `packages/opencode` and `packages/core`. - `oxlint` on changed files: 0 errors (4 pre-existing warnings in fs-util.ts unrelated to this change). ### Screenshots / recordings Not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: fix(patch): honor the end-of-file anchor when applying patches
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43331 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? The `*** End of File` anchor in update chunks never takes effect: `parseUpdateFileChunks` guards the change-line loop with `!lines[i].startsWith("***")`, so the `*** End of File` marker can never enter the loop body and `is_end_of_file` stays `undefined`. `tryMatch`'s EOF branch (match from end of file first) therefore never runs, and EOF-anchored patches edit the first occurrence of the pattern instead of the last. The reference parser in `packages/core/src/patch.ts` handles the marker correctly: its inner loop only excludes `@@`, checks the EOF marker in the body, and breaks on other `***` lines. This PR makes the opencode parser match that behavior. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added `should parse the end-of-file marker inside update chunks`: asserts `is_end_of_file: true` is parsed; fails before the fix, passes after. - Added `should match the end-of-file anchor against the last occurrence`: end-to-end test where a repeated `marker`/`end` pair is edited at the end of file only when the anchor is honored. - `bun test packages/opencode/test/patch/patch.test.ts`: 22 pass. Confirmed both new tests fail on the unfixed parser. - `@opencode-ai/opencode` typecheck passes. ### Screenshots / recordings _Not a UI change._ ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: fix(core): identify user-initiated web fetches
signal.text: ### Summary `webfetch` identified itself as Chrome 143 while sending a non-browser request profile. Meta's Comet routes classify that combination as an invalid browser request, returning a generic `500`; Facebook similarly returns `400`. Use a stable, transparent identity for user-initiated fetches instead: ```text Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; OpenCode-User/1.0; +https://opencode.ai ``` This follows the `ChatGPT-User` / `Claude-User` convention, avoids claiming to be ordinary Chrome, and preserves the format-specific `Accept` headers that let sites such as Cloudflare and Vercel serve Markdown directly. ### Verification - Meta geographic-use policy: old profile `500` (1,542-byte error), new profile `200` (313 KB HTML) - Facebook: old profile `400`, new profile `200` - Three repeated comparisons against Amazon, Stack Overflow, Reddit, old Reddit, Medium, Bloomberg, npm, and Reuters showed no status regression versus the old UA - Added assertions for the logical request profile and the actual headers received across both hops of a redirect - `bun test test/tool-webfetch.test.ts`: 52 pass - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core`: pass - Commit hook full-repository typecheck: 33 tasks pass

signal.title: fix(tui): settle completed shell state
signal.text: ## Summary - guarantee `shell.created` publishes before terminal lifecycle watchers and `shell.exited` publishes before shell waiters resolve - correlate shell inventory entries with their originating tool call - reconcile terminal shell removals reactively in the shared client data store - render completed foreground shell calls as settled and reserve the footer shell count for genuine background work ## Root cause Several lifecycle edges combined to leave the TUI looking busy after the assistant finished: 1. A fast process could emit `shell.exited` before `shell.created`. 2. Shell waiters could resolve before `shell.exited` was published, allowing the tool and assistant to complete first. 3. Completed foreground calls were inferred as background work from a retained shell ID alone. 4. The footer counted every cached shell instead of only calls whose terminal tool metadata says they remain running in the background. 5. A stale running tool projection could outlive its containing assistant step; foreground rendering now honors durable step completion. The resulting state matched #35816: the server reported no running shells while the mounted TUI retained a spinner and `1 shell` footer. ## Verification - deterministic core tests cover `created -> exited` ordering and prevent waiters resolving before exit publication - `bun test test/tool-shell.test.ts` in `packages/core` (25 pass) - `bun test test/cli/tui/data.test.tsx test/feature-plugins/prompt-footer.test.tsx` in `packages/tui` (42 pass) - package typechecks for core, client, and TUI - pre-push workspace typecheck (33 tasks successful) - visible standalone TUI verification in the Herdr `git-dummy` workspace: separate create, commit, and push shell calls completed; commit `2ac9eb0` reached `origin/main`; final `git push` row used the settled `$` marker with no spinner and no shell footer count Closes #35816.

signal.title: Managed ripgrep is unavailable to Shell commands recommended for exact match counts
signal.text: ### Description The built-in Grep tool description tells the model to use the Shell/Bash tool with `rg` when it needs an exact match count: > If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`. This can fail when ripgrep is not installed system-wide, even after OpenCode has successfully downloaded and can use its managed ripgrep binary. `RipgrepBinary` resolves or downloads `rg.exe`/`rg` into `Global.Path.bin`, and the built-in Grep/Glob tools invoke that binary by absolute path. The Shell tool, however, builds its environment from `process.env` plus plugin-provided variables and does not add `Global.Path.bin` to `PATH`. As a result, built-in Grep can work while a Shell command such as `rg --count pattern` fails with "command not found" / "not recognized". Relevant code on current `dev`: - `packages/opencode/src/tool/grep.txt` - `packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` Expected: either the OpenCode-managed ripgrep binary should be available to Shell commands recommended by built-in tool descriptions, or exact counting should be supported by the Grep tool so the prompt does not need to route the model through Shell. This is distinct from the offline bundling/download issues in #31734 and #34442: it can occur after the managed ripgrep download succeeds. #22820 previously reported the prompt-level symptom, but it was closed as obsolete when OpenCode no longer depended on ripgrep; current `dev` uses managed ripgrep again. ### Plugins None required. ### OpenCode version HEAD of `dev` at `7774461bbf7bd0600070cdede4fe8b9d9f301bf4`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start OpenCode in an environment where `rg`/`rg.exe` is not present in the system `PATH`. 2. Use the built-in Grep tool so OpenCode resolves/downloads its managed ripgrep binary. 3. Confirm the built-in Grep tool works. 4. Ask the agent for an exact match count, or run `rg --version` through the Shell tool. 5. Observe that Shell cannot resolve `rg`, despite the managed binary being available to built-in Grep. ### Operating System Cross-platform when system ripgrep is absent; especially visible on Windows. ### Terminal PowerShell, cmd.exe, or any shell whose inherited `PATH` does not contain ripgrep.

signal.title: [BUG]: checkPluginCompatibility silently skips when a plugin's package.json cannot be read
signal.text: ### Describe the bug `packages/opencode/src/plugin/shared.ts:194-205` validates `engines.opencode` against the running version and throws a precise error on mismatch: ```ts const range = engines.opencode if (typeof range !== "string") return if (!semver.satisfies(opencodeVersion, range)) { throw new Error(`Plugin requires opencode ${range} but running ${opencodeVersion}`) } ``` But the package read on the line above is `readPluginPackage(target).catch(() => undefined)`. An unreadable or malformed `package.json` yields `undefined`, the compatibility check is skipped entirely, and the plugin loads with no version gate and no signal. This is a compatibility gate whose own read failure disables the gate. The failure it exists to catch — a plugin running against an incompatible host — then proceeds silently, and the operator sees a plugin that loaded "fine" until something it depends on turns out to be missing. The cost is highest at a major-version boundary, which is exactly when the gate is load-bearing. Also worth stating in the same issue: the check no-ops when `semver.major(opencodeVersion) === 0` or the version is not valid semver, so dev builds are ungated. That may well be intentional, but it is currently implicit. ### Expected behavior An unreadable `package.json` for a plugin that is being loaded should surface — a warning naming the plugin at minimum, or a refusal to load. A gate that could not read its input should not report the same outcome as a gate that read its input and passed. Adjacent-correct behavior in the same function family, three lines below: every malformed *field* throws precisely (`invalid server export`, `must default export either server() or tui(), not both`). The field validation fails closed; the read failure fails open. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install a plugin whose `package.json` is unreadable or malformed (bad permissions, invalid JSON) while its entry module still resolves. 2. Load opencode with that plugin configured. 3. Observe the plugin loads with no compatibility check performed and no warning emitted — indistinguishable from a plugin that declared a satisfied `engines.opencode` range. Note: these steps are derived from the mechanism rather than from a recorded run — the finding came from reading the code path. ### Environment - Version: reproduces on current `dev` - Platform: Linux (not platform-specific) ### Additional context Found during an audit of fail-open paths — places where a `catch` inside a guard or cleanup path lets the guarded failure through silently — applied to this repo's plugin loader. The heuristic that produced it may be reusable: the defect usually sits beside a path that already handles the same condition correctly, so diffing a path against its own siblings surfaces the asymmetry. Here the sibling is the field validation in the same function. This matters more than usual right now because `engines.opencode` is the one mechanism that converts a silent plugin non-load into a thrown error naming the plugin — plugin authors are being advised to declare it precisely so an incompatible host announces itself rather than dropping the plugin's tools and guards silently. A gate that skips on an unreadable manifest undercuts that advice in the case where it is needed most.

signal.title: apply_patch: `*** End of File` anchor is dead code and never anchors to the end
signal.text:
### Bug description The `*** End of File` anchor in apply_patch updates is parsed but never takes effect: `packages/opencode/src/patch/index.ts` `parseUpdateFileChunks` guards the change-line loop with `!lines[i].startsWith("***")`, so the `*** End of File` line can never enter the loop body and `is_end_of_file` stays `undefined` forever. The `tryMatch` EOF branch (match from end of file first) therefore never runs, and EOF-anchored patches silently fall back to plain forward matching, editing the *first* occurrence of the pattern instead of the last. The reference parser in `packages/core/src/patch.ts` implements the same marker correctly (loop only excludes `@@`; the EOF marker is checked inside the body, and other `***` lines break the loop). ### Reproduction File `eof_anchor.txt` containing `marker
end
middle
marker
end` (no trailing newline), patch: ``` *** Begin Patch *** Update File: eof_anchor.txt @@ -marker -end +marker-changed +end *** End of File *** End Patch ``` Expected: last `marker` occurrence edited (`marker
end
middle
marker-changed
end`). Actual: first occurrence edited. ### Environment - OS: Windows - opencode version: dev branch

signal.title: Zen gateway (/go/v1) streaming: tool_calls continuation deltas send "id":null / "function":{"name":null} instead of omitting absent fields
signal.text: ### Description Streaming chat completions from the Zen gateway (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`) emit `tool_calls` continuation deltas with **explicit `null` values** for `id` and `function.name` instead of omitting the absent fields, as the OpenAI streaming format specifies. The first `tool_calls` delta of a call carries the real values, e.g.: ```json "delta":{"role":null,"content":"","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"chatcmpl-tool-b4d3cf2ed9145904","type":"function","function":{"name":"calculator","arguments":""}}]} ``` but every continuation delta for the same call sends: ```json "delta":{"role":null,"content":"","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":null,"type":null,"function":{"name":null,"arguments":""}}]} ``` This breaks strict OpenAI-compatible clients that accumulate deltas and treat any *present* field as an update. Concrete case: DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) accumulates `if (call.function?.name !== undefined) block.name = call.function.name` — the `null` overwrites the previously accumulated name, and every tool call ends up dispatched as `unknown tool ""`. The same request **non-streamed** returns a correct `message.tool_calls[]` with `id` and `function.name` intact. Observed model: `deepseek-v4-flash` (stream mode). The behavior is **intermittent across time windows** — client-side session logs show tool calls failing on 2026-08-17 ~04:34–12:08 UTC and 2026-08-19 ~02:37–02:50 UTC, while requests outside those windows (e.g., all of 2026-08-18) received spec-compliant chunks with the fields omitted. That pattern suggests different upstream backends behind the gateway, some of which emit `null`-filled deltas. ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version n/a — Zen gateway (`opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`), captured 2026-08-19 02:56 UTC ### Steps to reproduce ```bash curl -N https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Use the calculator tool to compute 2+2"}], "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"calculator","description":"compute an arithmetic expression","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"expr":{"type":"string"}},"required":["expr"]}}}], "tool_choice": "auto", "max_tokens": 200, "stream": true }' ``` The streamed SSE shows the chunk sequence quoted above: `id`/`name` present on the first `tool_calls` delta, explicit `null` on the continuation deltas. Expected: continuation deltas omit `id` / `type` / `function.name` when they carry no value (per the OpenAI streaming format), so field-presence-based delta accumulators keep the values from the first delta. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a (raw SSE text) ### Operating System macOS 25.5 (arm64), curl — issue is server-side

signal.title: Bug: MiMo V2.5 (mimo-v2.5) advertises video/audio support but video input is never received by the model
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary The OpenCode Go model `mimo-v2.5` advertises `text, image, audio, video` input capabilities (visible in `/models` and the model picker), but video input is never actually received by the model. The model responds "没收到" (didn't receive) regardless of format. ## Tested formats (all failed) All tested against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with model `mimo-v2.5`: 1. `{"type": "video_url", "video_url": "data:video/mp4;base64,..."}` → model replies it didn't receive any video 2. `{"type": "input_video", "video_url": {"url": "data:..."}}` → HTTP 503 "Endpoint is unavailable" 3. `{"type": "input_video", "video_url": "data:..."}` → model replies it didn't receive any video 4. `{"type": "video", "video": {...}}` and `{"type": "video", "video": "data:..."}` → model replies it didn't receive any video 5. Public HTTPS video URLs (e.g. MDN/W3Schools test videos) with `video_url` → model replies it didn't receive any video ## For comparison - `qwen3.7-plus` with `{"type": "video_url", "video_url": "data:video/mp4;base64,..."}` **works** — the model correctly describes the video content. - `kimi-k2.7-code` with the same format also works. - `mimo-v2.5` text input works fine (normal chat responses). ## Expected behavior Either video input should actually reach the model (per the advertised capabilities), or the metadata should not advertise video support. ## Actual behavior The model receives the message but no video content — the video modality is effectively non-functional despite being advertised. ### Plugins vision-auto-switch.ts (custom), ooclaw-opencode.js ### OpenCode version 1.18.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode Go subscription with API key 2. Send a chat completion request to https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions with model=mimo-v2.5 3. Include a video content part (any format: video_url string, input_video object, base64 data URL, or public HTTPS URL) 4. Observe: the model responds that it received no video 5. Repeat with qwen3.7-plus using identical video_url format → video is received and described correctly ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A (API-level bug, reproducible with plain curl) ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signal.title: bug: Azure DeepSeek V4 never selects the DeepSeek SDK adapter
signal.text: ## Summary Azure-hosted `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` deployments work through Chat Completions, but OpenCode's Azure provider cannot use the DeepSeek-specific AI SDK adapter. The models work only with their implicit default reasoning effort and custom `reasoningEffort` variants fail. ## Environment - OpenCode 1.18.18 - Windows 11 - Native `azure` provider with Azure AI Foundry DeepSeek V4 deployments - Global Standard deployments; no custom proxy or API key in config ## Reproduction 1. Deploy `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` or `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` in Azure AI Foundry. 2. Configure the model with `options.useCompletionUrls: true` so the base model uses Chat Completions. 3. Run the base model. It succeeds. 4. Add a model variant such as: ```json variants: { max: { reasoningEffort: max } } ``` 5. Run `opencode run --model azure/deepseek-v4-pro:max Reply" with exactly "OK`. ## Actual behavior The base model responds, but selecting a variant that passes `reasoningEffort` fails with a generic Azure server error. Direct Chat Completions calls to the same deployment accept `reasoning_effort: max` and return `reasoning_content` correctly. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` selects only `sdk.chat()` or `sdk.responses()` for the Azure provider. However, the bundled `@ai-sdk/azure` provider also exposes `sdk.deepseek()`. That adapter handles DeepSeek Chat Completions semantics, including `max_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`, and `reasoning_content` required across reasoning/tool-call turns. OpenCode never selects it. ## Expected behavior Azure DeepSeek models should use `sdk.deepseek(modelID)` when available, while retaining explicit API-routing overrides for non-DeepSeek Azure deployments. This would allow DeepSeek `low` / `high` / `max` reasoning effort and preserve reasoning content correctly in agentic multi-turn/tool-call sessions. ## Related - #29776 and PR #29775 covered generic Azure partner-model Chat Completions routing, but the PR was closed unmerged and did not select the DeepSeek-specific adapter. - #42147 covers Azure Responses API routing for OpenAI models. No credentials, resource names, or request IDs are included in this report.

signal.title: Deleting a session is slow/hangs, leaves ghost sessions, and can freeze the whole app
signal.text: ### Description Deleting a session in the desktop app is very slow, often hangs, and can freeze the entire app — with no error output in the logs. All three symptoms below appear to share one root cause: session removal (`removing share`) gets stuck. Observed symptoms (opencode 1.18.18 desktop, Windows 10): 1. **Deletion is slow / hangs.** A single deletion takes 10–30+ seconds; the UI becomes unresponsive. In the log (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\log\opencode.log`) consecutive `removing share` entries during a bulk delete of ~40 sessions show gaps of 6–28 seconds each. 2. **Ghost sessions.** If the app is killed during a deletion, the deleted session still appears on the home screen after restart. Clicking it opens the chat and immediately errors instead of loading. The interrupted removal apparently leaves the session in the local DB. 3. **Full freeze, silent.** The app sometimes stops logging entirely and must be force-killed. Three incidents today (local time): - 11:50 → 12:11 (21.8 min of silence) right after the bulk deletion above; - 16:02 → 16:17 (14.6 min, no graceful shutdown) right after opening/closing a terminal (`creating session` pty → `removing session`); - 16:26:31 (`exiting loop`) → 16:27:54 (`removing share`) → hung until killed at ~16:28:25. A normal shutdown logs `disposing all instances`; in the 16:02 incident that never appeared. No `level=ERROR`, no stack trace, no abort — pure silent hang. ### Plugins None (only the default `@opencode-ai/plugin` dependency in `~/.config/opencode/package.json`; no custom plugins or config) ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 (desktop app) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Delete a session from the home screen (single or multiple) 2. Observe that deletion takes tens of seconds or hangs the UI 3. If the app freezes, force-kill it and restart 4. The "deleted" session still appears on the home screen 5. Click that session → an error occurs instead of loading the chat 6. Optionally: open and close a terminal to reproduce the silent freeze ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Win11 ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: [BUG] Subagent final part lost — SessionProcessor.cleanup races with "removing share" (1.17.18)
signal.text: ### Description When a subagent (librarian / observer) session finishes, its final output doesn't show up in the TUI — the content just disappears. Digging into the logs, `SessionProcessor.cleanup` collides with the "removing share" flow when writing the final part. The ordering is the same across all 4 affected subagent sessions: 12:34:51 created ses_… subagent session created 12:34:51 loop / process / stream step 0..5 streaming fine 12:35:21 removing share ses_… ← this deletes the session + message rows 12:35:24 ERROR FOREIGN KEY constraint failed at Session.updatePart at SessionProcessor.cleanup ← cleanup tries to write part, parent rows already gone `Session.updatePart` does an upsert on `part`, whose FK points to `message(id)`. By the time cleanup runs, the parent `message` (and `session`) rows have already been deleted by the share-removal path, so the upsert trips the FK constraint and the whole part write gets rolled back. Net result: the subagent's last text / reasoning / step-start never lands in the DB, so the TUI has nothing to render for that turn. The DB itself is fine (`PRAGMA integrity_check` ok, no orphan parts / messages) — the content is just gone. ### Plugins oh-my-opencode-slim (same run also logged `Plugin export is not a function` for a `list` plugin, but the FK race reproduces independently of that ### OpenCode version 1.17.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start an orchestrator session and have it dispatch subagents (librarian / observer) that run a few steps and finish normally. 2. When the subagent session ends, opencode runs `removing share` (deletes the `session` + `message` rows) and *then* `SessionProcessor.cleanup` tries to upsert the final `part`. 3. `Session.updatePart` fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` because the parent `message` row no longer exists. 4. The subagent's final text / reasoning is never persisted → TUI renders nothing for that turn. Reproduced 6 FK failures across 4 subagent sessions in a single run today, all `deepseek-v4-flash`, all under run `e21ab353`. From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`: level=ERROR message=process session.id=ses_0a486e447ffe… error="Failed query: insert into \"part\" … (cause: SQLiteError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed)" at Session.updatePart at SessionProcessor.cleanup at SessionProcessor.process at SessionPrompt.run Afterward, all 4 `session.id`s and `messageID`s are missing from the DB; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns nothing — the failed upserts were rolled back, no dirty data, just lost parts. ### Screenshot and/or share link https://opncd.ai/share/vPVSWz88 The whole terminal fills up with what looks like TypeScript source code, as if someone opened a file in vim. As soon as I drag the mouse cursor across the terminal, the screen "tears" open and the real opencode TUI shows through underneath. Resizing the window fixes it for a while, but the moment I switch to another app/window and switch back, it reverts to the broken TS-code view. Feels like a redraw / alternate-screen-buffer issue — the TUI isn't repainting on focus regain, so stale terminal buffer content (left over from some tool output or editor) stays on screen until a mouse drag or resize forces a full repaint ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) ### Terminal Ghostty (xterm-ghostty)

signal.title: Bash tool hangs until timeout on Windows when spawned process keeps a stdout/stderr pipe open (dev servers, daemons)
signal.text: ### Description On Windows, the `bash` tool blocks until its timeout fires even though the requested command has effectively completed, whenever a spawned child/grandchild process stays alive **and** keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe open (e.g. `vite`, `uvicorn`, `npm run dev`). The tool waits for the stdout stream collector to terminate (pipe EOF), not just for the process to exit — so a long-lived process that holds the pipe write end means the call never resolves on its own. This appears to be the still-unfixed tail of a known chain: - #20902 — bash hangs when a command spawns background child processes (`close` vs `exit`). - #22012 — explicitly notes PR #20901 (v1.3.14) only fixed background processes that produce **no** output; continuously-outputting ones (uvicorn / npm run dev / docker compose up) still hang because the stdout stream collector never terminates. - #24784 — Windows-specific: grandchild inherits the stdout pipe handle, keeping the pipe open after the direct child exits. Filing this as a focused, reproducible **Windows + PowerShell** data point on top of those, since the existing reports are mostly Linux/WSL/bash framed and one of them (#24784) has no repro upvotes yet. ### What I observed (empirical, Windows 11 + PowerShell 5.1) Starting the same dev servers three different ways gives three different outcomes — the differentiator is purely **who holds the stdout/stderr pipe**: | Launch method | stdout/stderr destination | bash tool behavior | |---|---|---| | `node start.mjs` where the script does `spawn(cmd, args, { stdio: 'inherit' })` to start Vite | inherits the bash pipe | **Hangs to timeout** (Vite is long-lived → pipe never EOFs). Confirmed: call ended with `shell tool terminated command after exceeding timeout 60000 ms`, and the port was not actually LISTENing afterward. | | `Start-Process powershell ... -WindowStyle Hidden -RedirectStandardOutput out.log -RedirectStandardError err.log -PassThru` | redirected to files (not the bash pipe) | **Returns in <1s**, prints the wrapper PID. No hang. | | `run_in_background=true` on a dev server | inherits the bash pipe | Still never "completes" because the daemon never exits — background mode also waits on process end. | So on Windows the only reliable way to launch a persistent dev server without hanging the tool is to detach via `Start-Process` and redirect stdio to files, getting the pipe out of the loop entirely. ### Minimal reproduction (PowerShell) ```powershell # Hangs the bash tool until timeout: child keeps writing to the inherited stdout pipe powershell -Command "npm.cmd run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 28000" # Returns immediately: stdout/stderr redirected to files, pipe is never held by the daemon Start-Process powershell -ArgumentList '-NoProfile','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-Command','npm.cmd run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 28000' -WindowStyle Hidden -RedirectStandardOutput out.log -RedirectStandardError err.log -PassThru ``` (Equivalent with `python -m uvicorn app:app --port 8765` in place of the npm command.) ### Expected vs actual - **Expected:** once the foreground command's own work is done (or for a daemon, once it has started), the tool should resolve based on process `exit` rather than blocking on stream/pipe EOF held by a surviving child. - **Actual:** the tool stays `running` until the timeout kills it, because the stdout stream collector waits for the pipe write end to close, which a long-lived child never does. ### Suggested direction (matching #22012 / #20902 discussion) Don't gate completion on the stdout/stderr stream collector finishing. Resolve on process `exit` and stop reading the pipe shortly after exit (e.g. a short grace window post-`exit`), so a surviving grandchild holding the pipe can't keep the tool execution promise pending. This generalizes the partial `close`→`exit` fix from PR #20901 to the continuously-outputting case. ### Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Shell: Windows PowerShell 5.1 - Node: v25.2.1, npm 11.6.2 - Python: 3.11.7 (uvicorn case) - Frameworks reproduced with: Vite 5.4 (`npm run dev`), FastAPI/uvicorn 0.32 ### Related - #20902 - #22012 - #24784 - PR #20901

signal.title: V2: add origin-aware reasoning metadata replay handling
signal.text: ## Context Reasoning signatures and similar opaque replay artifacts are tied to the provider/API/model path that produced them. Reusing them after switching provider, API, or model can make the next request invalid. ## Scope - Model assistant-message origin/compatibility identity for opaque replay artifacts. - Let protocol compilers replay compatible metadata and strip or lower incompatible metadata. - Start with Anthropic reasoning signatures and Bedrock/Vertex Anthropic compatibility concerns. - Avoid making callers manually inspect provider metadata bags. ## Acceptance Criteria - Same-origin continuation can replay compatible reasoning metadata. - Switching incompatible provider/API/model paths drops or lowers invalid replay artifacts. - Tests cover same-origin continuation and incompatible model/provider switching.
